#5391. Crypto Stocks Lost Up to 54% in October as Hedge Funds Erased Every AI Stock Purchase Since 2025: Why Did Bitcoin Miners Fall Hardest?

Crypto stocks start November after an October that cost them up to 54%, more than six times Bitcoin’s drop, as Goldman Sachs data showed hedge funds sold enough AI stocks in five sessions to wipe out all their net AI buying since early 2025.

That matters for crypto because the biggest losers weren’t the exchanges. They were Bitcoin miners, which have spent two years renting their power and data centres to AI companies and now trade like AI infrastructure.

Cipher Digital (CIFR) fell 53.9% between the September 30 and October 30 closes, and IREN lost 41.4%. MARA and Riot dropped 40.2% and 36.4%. Bitcoin, tracked by BlackRock’s IBIT, fell 8.4% over the same days, and the S&P 500 barely moved.

The exchanges caught up later. Coinbase and Robinhood held up through the hedge fund selling streak, then lost 17% and 16% in the second half of the month, much of it on Friday after the Binance hack and Coinbase’s results.

So were crypto stocks sold as crypto, or as AI?

JUST IN: Hedge funds are pulling money out of US stocks at fastest pace ever

Hedge funds sold AI stocks for five straight sessions, from October 8 to 14, on Goldman Sachs’ prime brokerage data. Most of it was funds dumping shares they already owned, about 3.5 times the pace of new short bets, and roughly $20 billion of tech stock went out over two weeks.

Goldman Delta-One head Rich Privorotsky put the problem in one line: computing demand “can grow exponentially, but the capital available to finance it cannot.”

That line describes the miners. Cipher, IREN, Hut 8, TeraWulf and Core Scientific have all signed deals to host AI computing, and IREN’s AI cloud revenue of $70.5 million overtook its Bitcoin mining revenue of $66.7 million for the first time last quarter.

The selling streak shows who traded as what. From the October 7 close to October 14:

Every miner fell harder than chip stocks in the week hedge funds dumped AI, Cipher more than three times as hard, while Bitcoin hardly moved.

The miners, then the trading venues, then the Bitcoin holders. Over the full month, the order lines up with how much of each business looks like AI or trading volume, and how little looks like Bitcoin itself.

Strategy is the tell. A company that is mostly a pile of Bitcoin fell in line with chip stocks (-14.2%), not with miners, and Circle, which earns interest on stablecoin reserves, fell least of all.

The trading venues had their own problem. Most of Coinbase’s and Robinhood’s losses came after October 14, once the hedge fund streak was over, and Friday alone took 10.6% off Coinbase and 7.2% off Robinhood.

The timing points to AI money for the miners, though it is no proof: Bitcoin’s own 8% slide and a weaker hashprice cut into their mining revenue too.

Discover: Oil Prices Climb Back Above $110 While Crypto Stocks Lose Up to 48% in a Month: Miners Are Falling Even Faster

IREN is the clearest test of the AI trade among crypto stocks, and it reports fiscal first-quarter results on Thursday, November 5. The stock closed Friday at $23.95, down 8.8% on the day, after touching $23.06, its lowest in a year.

The daily chart shows a stock that lost its floor. The July 29 low at $28.93 held through the summer, gave way on October 15, and turned into the ceiling: IREN’s bounce stalled at $28.88 on October 28 and fell the next two days.

May 12 to October 30, 2026: IREN 1D chart. Source: Yahoo Finance (Nasdaq).

Both averages are far above. The 50-day EMA (exponential moving average) sits at $35.64 and the 200-day at $40.82, and the 50-day crossed below the 200-day on September 30, just before the selling began.

For crypto stocks, Thursday is the first chance to see whether AI customers are still paying the miners, or whether October’s selling was right about the capital running out.

#5390. Ledger CTO Sounds Alarm Over New Cryptographic Threats to Bitcoin

Two new cryptographic breakthroughs raise concerns over the future of Bitcoin (BTC) and other cryptocurrencies, according to Ledger Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet.

According to Guillemet's Oct. 30 post on X, a recent study shows that it might be easier to break the mathematics behind elliptic-curve cryptography (ECC), which is how Bitcoin is secured.

“Thought it was a bad week for crypto? You may have missed the real news,” wrote Guillemet.

Elliptic-curve cryptography works by making it practically impossible to solve the elliptic-curve discrete logarithm problem.

So far, the best general method to solve it has been Pollard’s rho algorithm. Its computational cost increases exponentially with key size.

Now, the researchers have presented a subexponential algorithm that might in theory solve it more efficiently.

There is a big caveat. It relies on another claim by OpenAI researchers that requires further investigation.

The new algorithm doesn’t put current cryptographic schemes at risk, Guillemet insisted.

The best attacks for popular curves, like secp256k1 for Bitcoin, NIST P-256 and Ed25519, are still based on Pollard’s rho.

The new one would only be more efficient for hypothetical curves of very large sizes. For now, it’s just theoretical.

The second breakthrough is a big advance in the efficiency of quantum computing attacks on elliptic-curve cryptography.

Guillemet referenced a public research project, ECDSA.fail, aimed at improving the efficiency of quantum computing attacks against elliptic-curve digital signatures.

Researchers managed to reduce the estimated quantum circuit cost by about 70% relative to what Google previously reported, the Ledger executive explained.

Current estimates put the cost at about 0.91 billion in the logical-qubit-times-Toffoli-gates metric, down from 2.99 billion in Google’s figures.

What’s more important is that the French quantum computing company Alice & Bob has published a new paper estimating that it’s theoretically possible to break Bitcoin's secp256k1 cryptography using fewer than 30,000 physical cat qubits in about an hour.

The same paper estimates that factoring RSA-2048 would require 22,593 cat qubits and take about 3.14 days.

Such a quantum computer does not exist, so there is no immediate risk to Bitcoin, Guillemet noted.

However, these findings are a reminder of how the estimated resources needed to break common cryptographic schemes keep shrinking.

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Bitcoin price fell sharply as renewed Iran conflict fears collided with a wave of crypto hacks, giving us a fresh market shock. Reports of US strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island revived concerns about oil supplies, while a string of security breaches continued to undermine confidence across the digital asset industry.

The sell-off comes as we are grappling with weak crypto sentiment, falling ETF flows and uncertainty surrounding global markets. Bitcoin is now caught between geopolitical risk and a growing security crisis within its own industry.

The latest reported US strikes added uncertainty to an eight-month conflict that has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices edged higher after the reports, with Brent crude trading near $105 per barrel today.

The Iran narrative returned to the forefront after reports that US forces struck Qeshm Island, near the Strait of Hormuz. The US officials themself described the strikes as defensive, but the development threatens to complicate diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran. The two sides have continued contacts aimed at ending the conflict, but no breakthrough has emerged.

❗️ US OFFICIALS CONFIRMED WASHINGTON BOMBED IRAN'S QESHM ISLAND FEW HOURS AGO IN A SERIES OF 'LIMITED STRIKES' — WSJ pic.twitter.com/Yy3C0ysWPQ

The Strait of Hormuz remains a major concern for global markets. The waterway previously carried around one-fifth of global oil and natural gas supplies, making any disruption a potential threat to energy prices and inflation.

Higher oil price could complicate the outlook for central banks and keep financial conditions tight. That would leave risk assets, including Bitcoin, vulnerable if investors shift toward cash and safer investments.

Asian equities also retreated today as investors weighed geopolitical risks, technology-sector weakness and uncertainty ahead of US midterm elections. Reuters reported that MSCI’s Asia-Pacific index excluding Japan fell 1.4%, while South Korean shares dropped as much as 4.1%.

Rather than acting as a safe haven, BTC has continued to trade like a risk-sensitive asset during periods of market stress.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

The geopolitical shock arrives as crypto investors are still processing one of the industry’s largest security incidents. Binance suffered a breach involving $6.3 billion in crypto assets. Customers withdrew billions of dollars following the incident, raising questions about confidence in centralized trading platforms.

The exchange said it would cover the losses, while withdrawals later began stabilizing. However, the incident has added another source of uncertainty for traders already navigating a fragile market.

The Binance breach is not an isolated case. Recent attacks have also hit Mercado Bitcoin, Polymarket and infrastructure providers serving crypto platforms.

Mercado Bitcoin disclosed a security incident involving customer-related systems, while Polymarket experienced unauthorized withdrawals through a compromised third-party provider. The incidents have renewed concerns about the security of exchanges, wallets, and services connected to crypto applications.

A wave of attacks has also targeted older BTCPay Server installations and a vulnerable WordPress crypto-payment plugin, according to recent security reports.

The timing is particularly damaging. Crypto markets need fresh capital and confidence to sustain a recovery, but repeated breaches risk pushing investors toward self-custody or away from the sector altogether.

Read More: Binance Hacked For Billions, Funds SAFU?

Bitcoin price now depends on whether geopolitical tensions ease and crypto-specific fears begin to fade. A diplomatic breakthrough between the US and Iran could reduce pressure on oil markets and improve appetite for risk assets. However, another escalation around the Strait of Hormuz could renew inflation concerns and trigger further selling across equities and crypto.

Bitcoin also needs to show that the recent security incidents have not triggered a deeper withdrawal of capital from the industry. Binance’s outflows and the latest exchange breaches will remain important sentiment indicators.

For now, the Iran story is unfolding alongside a wider Bitcoin and crypto confidence test. If the sell-off continues, Bitcoin could face another challenge to its recovery. If geopolitical fears cool and the hacking fallout remains contained, buyers may get an opportunity to step back in.

Can BTC stabilize despite pressure from both global markets and the industry’s own security failures?

To stabilize at all, Bitcoin first needs to reclaim $78,000. Even then, heavier resistance is waiting between $80,000 and $82,000, where several moving averages bunch together.

#5387. Citi Raises Bitcoin Target to $113,000, Sees $181,000 Within 12 Months

Citi has revised its price targets for the pioneer cryptocurrency, believing the asset is poised to reclaim $113,000 and even hit $181,000 in the next 12 months.

US Wall Street bank Citi Group made a fresh bold prediction on Bitcoin’s price, now convinced that the asset is set to reach $113,000 before 2027. The $1.2 trillion bank believes the flagship cryptocurrency will rise to $113,000 before the end of the year.

Today, October 1, Citi amended its 12-month Bitcoin price projection from $82,000 to $113,000, a significant shift in its market outlook earlier this year. The latest revision signals the institution’s renewed confidence in the Bitcoin market, supported by positive macroeconomic forces and ETF inflows expected through this year and into 2027.

In January, the bank predicted a price target of $143,000 within the next 12 months. In July, it cut its target from $112,000 to $82,000 when the CLARITY Act lost its momentum in the Senate. During that time, the institution decreased its target, saying that the asset could drop from $112,000 to $82,000 due to negative developments, including consistent ETF outflows, the US’s delayed regulation formulation, and a wider stagnant market.

The latest forecast, issued today, shows that the bank has turned bullish on Bitcoin, believing that the asset is preparing to extend its ongoing recovery in the fourth quarter. While the asset closed Q3 around $82,000, Citi believes the virtual currency is gearing up for a momentum Q4 rally and could reach $113,000 before 2027. The bank expects institutional capital to soon surge into digital assets, suggesting BTC is entering its next bull-run phase.

The Wall Street banking giant expects crypto capital inflows to rise to $5 billion within the next 12 months, driven by the broader market recovery. As a result, the bank believes that Bitcoin’s value could hit $181,000 in the coming 12 months. This price forecast reflects its strong belief that traditional financial institutions are increasingly channeling capital onchain.

Citi’s analysts said Bitcoin is attracting significantly more institutional customers amid economic uncertainty. With heightened institutional demand, major participants like corporate treasuries, pension funds, hedge funds, and others are showing stronger enthusiasm for BTC as a long-term investment.

Citi is convinced that if this momentum continues, BTC could begin a new chapter of adoption, where it’s not only widely used for trading but also as a reserve asset. This transition could push its value to unprecedented heights, with $181,000 a realistic target over the next 12 months.

#5386. Bitcoin Sellers Take a Week of Losses Below $80,000 as Strategy and Strive Keep Buying: Will $75,000 Hold?

Bitcoin (BTC) sellers booked their longest run of daily losses since mid-August last week, Glassnode said on Monday, November 2, as Strategy and Strive added 935 BTC between them, though Strategy spent three times as much buying back its own preferred stock.

Strategy bought 811 BTC for $65.5 million, at an average of $80,846, taking its stash to 849,327 BTC. The same filing shows $208.2 million going into STRC, the preferred stock Strategy sells to fund its purchases, which has been trading just under its $100 face value.

Strive bought 124 BTC for $10 million at $80,526 each, chief executive Matt Cole posted, bringing it to 43,124 BTC. For the first time, part of it was paid for by selling SATS, Strive’s own preferred stock.

Both companies bought above today’s price. Bitcoin trades at $77,948, below the $80,000 line where Glassnode says sellers have been accepting losses all week.

In August and September, the same kind of selling marked the bottom. So are sellers close to done again, or is the treasury buying too small to matter?

bitcoin:native sellers have been taking losses below $80k.Last week brought the longest run of daily net realized losses since mid-August.The August and September loss clusters both formed at the local lows. A hold above $75k would fit that pattern. pic.twitter.com/DCjbNfhoT7

A pattern that has twice marked a low. Glassnode tracks realized profit and loss, the gain or loss on each coin when it moves, against the price it last moved at. Since the October 29 Binance hack sent BTC under $80,000, the losses have outweighed the profits almost every day.

The firm’s chart, titled “Profit Taking Is Slowing Down,” marks the earlier loss clusters:

The logic is simple. Sellers who accept a loss are usually the ones who bought high and gave up, and once they are out, there are fewer coins left to dump.

“A hold above $75k would fit that pattern,” Glassnode wrote.

Two clusters in three months is a short record, though, and the August one came at a much lower price. The pattern only holds if buyers show up, which brings in the companies.

Its filings don’t say, but the price points to one reason. STRC is built to trade close to $100, and it closed Friday at $99.13. Strategy’s November 2 filing shows it bought back 2.09 million shares for $208.2 million, about $99.52 each.

That has become the bigger job. Over the last five weekly filings, Strategy spent $974.9 million on STRC and $137.8 million on BTC.

The board has topped up the buyback program by about $1 billion since mid-October, leaving $748.6 million to spend. Strategy now holds 849,327 BTC at an average cost of $75,451, about 3% below the current price.

Mostly with cash it already had. Strive’s 124 BTC came a week after it bought 6,182 BTC for $511.4 million, so the pace has dropped sharply.

The new part is SATS, Strive’s preferred stock. Its sales program was used for the first time, and all of the week’s program proceeds came from it rather than from ASST common shares, which fell 28% between October 21 and 30.

Cole also put Strive’s amplification ratio at 62.7%. That is its debt and preferred stock against the value of its BTC, so the lower the price, the higher it climbs. At Friday’s $76,764, Strive’s 43,124 BTC were worth $3.31 billion.

Discover: Bitcoin Rebound Faces a Test in Strategy’s STRC Funding

So far, it has held higher. BTC trades at $77,948 on Binance, down 0.5% on the day, and has stayed above its October 30 low of $76,326 for three days. That low sits right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average) at $76,510.

Both treasury companies bought above here, at $80,846 and $80,526, which is roughly where the 50-day EMA now caps the price at $80,287.

August 5 to November 2, 2026: BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: Binance.

For Bitcoin, the test is the one Glassnode set: if $75,000 holds while the loss-takers finish, last week will look like August and September again.

One concerning development is the increase in trading volume that comes with SHIB's recent price declines. The latest daily candlesticks show stronger selling activity as the token approaches the $0.00000460–$0.00000480 support region.

SHIB's moving-average structure also remains unfavorable. The cryptocurrency trades below several important moving averages, including its longer-term trend indicator.

Unless SHIB reclaims its overhead moving averages and attracts stronger buying volume, the path of least resistance appears to remain downward.

#5384. Reconciling the OCC’s Final Stablecoin Reserve Floors Against the Fed’s Proposal

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

The OCC's final GENIUS Act rule sets a 5% cash floor and a 40% cap on any one counterparty. The Fed's open proposal uses neither figure, and its comment window runs until November 30.

Issuers now face two sets of reserve rules that share a redemption deadline and differ on almost everything else.

Ask a stablecoin issuer what its reserves must look like in 2027, and the honest answer is now: it depends which regulator you ask.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) gave its answer on October 21, the final rule implementing the GENIUS Act. Our October 19 piece on staggered agency filings expected that rule "before the end of October," and it came two days later. The rule sets specific numbers: at least 5% of reserves in demand deposits or similar instant-access funds, and no more than 40% of reserves with a single counterparty.

The Federal Reserve's answer is still a proposal. Its GENIUS Act rulemaking remains open for comment until November 30, and it contains neither of those numbers. Until the Fed finalizes its rule, any company planning to issue under both agencies' rules, or deciding which one to apply to, is working with one fixed set of numbers and one open-ended set of principles.

The OCC's final rule was published in the Federal Register on October 23 and takes effect on January 18, 2027, the same day as the GENIUS Act itself. Comptroller Jonathan V. Gould called it "a clear, practical framework for payment stablecoin innovation, with strong standards for reserve backing, redemption, and risk management."

The reserve rules are looser than the March proposal in several places:

The OCC also removed the rebuttable presumption that some affiliate yield arrangements break the GENIUS Act's ban on paying interest, though it kept its broader anti-evasion powers. The agency received about 328 comments.

For existing issuers, the timeline is short. Under OCC Bulletin 2026-51, firms already operating in the United States that file a "substantially complete" application by January 18 can generally expect a waiver of the prior-approval requirement.

The Fed released its two proposals on September 24. They were published in the Federal Register on September 29 under Docket No. R-1899, and comments are due November 30.

The main requirements proposal would require Board-supervised issuers to "fully back their stablecoins with certain permissible reserve assets". The reserves' fair value would have to equal or exceed the stablecoins' outstanding value at all times. Permissible assets include:

On diversification, however, the Fed sets no numbers. Reserves must be "sufficiently diverse" to keep one-to-one backing at all times, and issuers must manage concentration in uninsured deposits and repo counterparties. The Board says it generally expects reserves to be mostly Treasuries, but it sets no cash floor and no counterparty percentage.

Redemption is where the two agencies agree most closely. Both define timely redemption as no later than two business days after a request. The difference lies in what happens under stress.

The FDIC, in its own proposal, uses a third approach: issuers would report on their own when redemption requests exceed 10% of issuance within 24 hours.

The clearest conflict is not about how much cash an issuer must hold, but how each agency treats bank deposits.

Under the OCC rule, at least 5% of reserves must be held in demand deposits or similar balances. That is a direct requirement to hold bank money.

The Fed proposal has no deposit floor. Instead, it would charge 2% capital against reserves held as uninsured deposits at an insured bank, and the same charge applies to undercollateralized reverse repo. One agency requires a minimum amount in deposits, and the other makes issuers hold extra capital against the deposits they choose to keep.

Concentration works the same way. An issuer with 60% of its deposit reserves at one bank would breach the OCC's 40% cap, unless one of the custodian or government exemptions applies. Under the Fed's current text, that issuer would face only a judgment by its supervisor about whether it has managed concentration risk properly.

The rules for a reserve shortfall also differ:

The difference is largest on capital. The OCC sets an individualized capital requirement measured in GAAP tangible equity. It has a $5 million floor that now lasts for the issuer's whole life, plus an operational backstop equal to 12 months of total expenses, up to half of which can be funded with qualifying subordinated debt.

The Fed proposes a fixed formula. On top of the 2% charges on deposits and repo, it adds an operational-risk charge on outstanding issuance:

It also adds 25% of three-year average revenue from sources other than reserves, adjusted by a loss scalar.

For an issuer with $50 billion in circulation, the issuance charge alone works out to $850 million under the Fed's proposal, before the revenue add-on. The OCC rule has no comparable fixed figure. Its capital depends on the issuer's own risk profile, with the $5 million floor as the only set minimum.

For now, the OCC's figures are final and the Fed's are not. Issuers and banks that hold reserves can still argue for changes until the Fed's comment period closes on November 30, and the Fed has asked 277 questions.

The decisions that matter most are clear from the comparison above:

Both sets of rules apply from the same date, January 18, 2027. If the Fed's final rule keeps its current approach, the United States will begin regulating stablecoins with a common redemption deadline and two different reserve rulebooks, decided by which agency charters the issuer.

#5383. Why November's +80% History Is a Statistical Flaw for XRP Holders

XRP's 15.7% drop in October has brought the token to the most unpredictable crossroads of the year. Historical data from thirteen years of observations promise the market harsh November volatility. However, behind the optimistic figures of past years lies a serious methodological flaw capable of disorienting investors amid the current pressure.

The main trap for the market is the asymmetry of returns. According to Cryptorank, XRP's average November gain is an impressive +80.2%, but this figure is completely distorted by two isolated anomalies: a surge of +531.9% in 2013 and a rally of +281.7% in 2024. The month's median, a negative -10%, reflects reality much more accurately.

Historically, in most cycles, XRP closed November in the red. The fourth quarter, which so far consists of October alone, is already down -16.3%, in line with the asset's seasonal tendency toward correction that the averaged statistics mask.

The median is not a perfect guide either: thirteen observations are a small sample, and the market structure has changed. Since spot XRP ETFs launched in the US in mid-November 2025, the token has had an institutional demand channel that did not exist in earlier cycles.

Mathematical pessimism is reinforced by the real balance of power on the market at the end of October. The XRP price has fallen below the key support line of $1.30 and is trading around $1.25–$1.26, marking a local downtrend.

All the upward momentum built on investors' expectations has faded, opening the way for profit-taking by short-term players. Notably, the October decline follows a 48% gain in the third quarter, XRP's best Q3 in four years, which suggests that at least part of the current pressure is profit-taking after the rally rather than seasonality alone.

The situation is aggravated by an inevitable influx of supply amid a liquidity shortage. On Sunday, November 1, a scheduled unlock of 1 billion XRP from Ripple's escrow wallets will take place.

It is worth noting, however, that the escrow unlock is a routine monthly event that has followed the same schedule since 2017, and Ripple typically returns 600–800 million XRP to new escrow contracts. The real net addition to circulating supply is therefore closer to 200–400 million XRP.

Even so, against the backdrop of thin liquidity, this volume is enough to put additional pressure on the price, as it will enter the market simultaneously with macroeconomic pressure and the aftermath of the recent wave of forced liquidations of long positions worth more than $1.29 billion, caused by a security incident at the Binance exchange.

At the same time, the wave of liquidations has partially cleared excess leverage from the market. If funding rates stay negative and open interest does not recover, the bearish scenario may be capped by a short squeeze, which would make a retest of $1.30–$1.32 more likely than the statistics suggest.

#5382. XRP Reserves on Binance Hit Lowest Level Since 2022

As the broader crypto market continues to face intense selling pressure due to the prolonged market volatility seen over the past weeks, XRP appears to be seeing rising demand instead.

While its price is also struggling amid the market downturn, onchain data from crypto analytics platform CryptoQuant shows that more tokens are leaving major exchanges instead, which could be interpreted as intense buying.

The data shows that XRP reserves on the world's largest exchange by volume, Binance, have dropped to their lowest level since December 2022.

As of October 30, Binance has seen its XRP reserve fall to 2.47 billion XRP from the 2.69 billion XRP it recorded on October 28, marking a sharp decline in its holdings in just two days.

This signals rapid accumulation from traders as it marks a decrease of about 8.18% in the amount of XRP available for sale on Binance, with over  220 million XRP withdrawn in just a two-day period.

While decreases in exchange reserves simply mean a reduction in the amount of XRP readily available for trading, it potentially reduces immediate selling pressure if demand remains steady, thereby providing a bullish outlook for the token.

Further data shows that the decrease in the XRP exchange reserve on Binance has coincided with falling XRP balances on several other major crypto exchanges, including Bybit and Bithumb.

The data shows that reductions seen on these exchanges were smaller compared to Binance, as Bybit's XRP reserves dropped from 306 million to 286 million XRP during the same period.

Bithumb, on the other hand, also recorded a decrease of 10 million XRP, with its reserves falling from 1.847 billion to 1.837 billion XRP, down approximately 0.54% during the same days.

While this indicates a broader reduction in exchange-held supply and XRP has remained volatile despite the shrinking supply, it is important to note that lower balances do not always mean that investors are accumulating XRP, which could be the reason XRP has yet to react to the trend.

Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz has revealed the unexpected story behind an iconic XRP-themed T-shirt he wore at the Swell event, explaining how a technical milestone on the XRP Ledger became associated with a memorable price moment.

Schwartz, one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger (XRPL), was spotted wearing a T-shirt that showed a 'speedometer'-like inscription that pointed to 100, sparking curiosity among members of the XRP community.

X user @unknowDLT had asked Schwartz about the origin of the T-shirt he wore in an image that accompanied his tweet. "At this point, could you clearly explain what the T-shirt you're wearing means?" he asked.

@unknowDLT It was created to commemorate XRPL hitting 100 TPS. When we commissioned it, XRP was around 30 cents. By the time we got it, XRP was $1. So everyone thought that's what XRP at 100 meant and we just went with it.

Schwartz responded that the T-shirt was created to commemorate XRPL hitting 100 TPS. "When the T-shirt was commissioned, XRP was around 30 cents. By the time we got it, XRP was $1," Schwartz further explained.

The timing caused some members of the XRP community to assume the "100" on the shirt referred to XRP reaching a price of $1 rather than the network's transaction speed.

"So everyone thought that's what XRP at 100 meant and we just went with it," Schwartz added.

In the X discussion, the Ripple CTO Emeritus did not share exact details on the time when the T-shirt was commissioned.

XRP also traded around 30 cents ($0.30) at several points in its price history, so it may be hard to know exactly when, in the context of the Ripple CTO Emeritus's post. A walk-through of the XRP Ledger throughput chronology may provide a hint.

When performance testing began in February 2015, the XRP Ledger sustained 80 transactions per second. Incremental improvements were made over time as opportunities were uncovered.

Between March and June 2015, the XRP Ledger sustained between 120 and 490 transactions per second. In October 2015, XRPL saw a major throughput boost to 525 transactions per second, and in the following year, this nearly doubled to 1,100 transactions per second.

In July 2017, XRP was demonstrated to sustain a throughput of 1,500 transactions per second, which remains so to this day.

#5380. Exchange Ledgers in the Middle as CFTC and SEC Diverge on What “Delivery” Means

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

A customer buys a token on a U.S. exchange and the app shows the balance. Under the CFTC's December 14 framework, nothing has been delivered yet.

Under the SEC's crypto proposal, delivery doesn't decide the question at all. An October 27 comment letter asks the two agencies to settle on one answer.

Open almost any crypto exchange app after a purchase and you'll see a clean number: 1.0000 ETH, available. To the customer, the asset is theirs. To the exchange's database, it's a row in an internal ledger. To federal regulators, that row is now being judged by two different tests that don't agree on what it means.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on what it calls Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (CAM). It sets out the agency's first formal view of "actual delivery" for crypto since it withdrew its 2020 guidance last December. Comments close on December 14.

The Securities and Exchange Commission's Regulation Crypto Assets proposal takes a different view of the same moment. Then, on October 27, a comment letter on the SEC's file raised the gap directly. It described the situation as "two conflicting definitions of the same physical facts" and asked the agencies to "please coordinate the definitions."

Delivery matters because it decides which rulebook applies.

For the CFTC, the answer comes from Section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act. A leveraged, margined or financed retail commodity trade is treated like a futures contract unless "actual delivery" happens within 28 days. If delivery happens in time, the trade falls outside futures rules. If it doesn't, the exchange is effectively running a futures venue.

For the SEC, the question is whether a token is still part of an investment contract. Under the August proposal, a covered investment contract ends when the issuer has finished or permanently stopped its essential managerial efforts and files a Form TR transition report. Whether the buyer has received the token is not part of that test.

So one agency treats delivery as the deciding question, and the other barely considers it.

The CFTC's position is still preliminary, but it is detailed. Published in the Federal Register on October 13, the notice relies on the Monex case standard: actual delivery requires "the transfer of some meaningful degree of possession or control."

For crypto, the agency suggests that possession and control "may require possession of the credentials (e.g., private key(s))." It takes three positions that matter most to exchanges:

The agency is also asking whether control has to be exclusive, whether delivery can happen while a lien or security interest is outstanding, and how financing offered in an exchange's standard account documents affects whether a trade is covered at all.

The SEC's proposal, released on August 18, deals with a different question. It creates offering exemptions, including a $5 million startup exemption over four years, and a safe harbor for when a crypto asset's investment contract ends. Neither depends on where the token sits.

Under the proposal, a token held in a customer's self-custody wallet and a token recorded on an exchange's books are treated the same way. In both cases, the investment contract question depends on the issuer's managerial efforts and its filings.

That is the gap the October 27 letter tries to close. Its author, who describes themselves as a fintech founder designing a consumer platform, argues that "where the customer holds the private keys or execution is on-chain, with custody evidence, the asset should be treated as delivered and the covered-investment-contract analysis should end there."

Running four common exchange transactions through both frameworks shows where the tests split.

Trade one: a fully paid purchase left on the exchange.

Trade two: the same purchase withdrawn to a self-custody wallet on day three.

Trade three: a margined purchase kept on the exchange's ledger for 30 days.

Trade four: an on-chain swap that settles directly into the user's wallet.

The pattern is consistent. Self-custody is the only position that clearly counts as delivery under the CFTC's view and also ends the analysis under the letter's proposed SEC fix. Everything left on an exchange's internal ledger stays in an unclear position. The CFTC treats it as undelivered and the SEC's text doesn't address it.

The letter was filed on October 27, a week after the SEC's October 20 comment deadline. It is anonymous and brief, but its main concern is practical. If the definitions stay separate, it warns, founders will have to design products around whichever rule is stricter.

It is the only filing on either docket so far that sets the two definitions side by side.

The CFTC process is still at the advance-notice stage, so a formal proposal will follow. For U.S. platforms, though, the direction is clear. Under the CFTC's preliminary reading, an exchange that keeps customer assets in internal ledger accounts has not delivered them. If that exchange also offers margin or financing, it is on track to be treated as a futures venue.

The SEC's final rule could adopt the letter's custody-based approach or keep delivery out of its analysis entirely. Until one of those happens, the same ledger entry can be undelivered for one regulator and irrelevant for the other.

Exchanges and their customers have until December 14 to say which definition should prevail. The real decision is whether "delivered" ends up meaning the same thing at both agencies.

#5377. Crypto and Midterm Election: 3 Risks From Trump’s $5,000 Stimulus to Iran

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Crypto is facing a major political test as Americans head to the polls on November 3, with the US midterm election potentially reshaping regulation, stimulus expectations, and investor risk appetite.

Republicans are fighting to retain control of Congress, while Democrats are seeking to regain power in at least one chamber. The outcome could determine if President Donald Trump advances his economic agenda or faces a tougher legislative road ahead.

For crypto, the midterm election comes with three major risks: Trump’s proposed $5,000 stimulus dividend, the future of stalled crypto legislation, and escalating tensions with Iran.

The election itself may not immediately change Crypto’s fundamentals. However, it could shift expectations around liquidity, regulation, and the financial markets.

Trump has promised a $5,000 dividend payment to adult US citizens if Republicans retain control of both the House and Senate. The proposal would cover 240 million adults, potentially costing around $1.2 trillion, and Trump has also suggested that tariff revenue could help fund the payments.

Trump may have just sealed the deal on stage in Dallas.He's promising a $5,000 dividend to every American adult if Republicans win the midterms — only condition is the money has to be spent in the U.S.I've never seen anything like this. pic.twitter.com/ypJP2fYsLj

A Republican victory could then strengthen expectations for additional household spending and potentially inject fresh liquidity into financial markets. We, in the crypto market, have historical reasons to watch stimulus closely.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, US stimulus checks coincided with extraordinary monetary easing and a powerful crypto rally. A Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland study found that the 2020 payments increased Bitcoin buy volume by 3.8%, while the associated price effect was modest.

The 2020–2021 rally also benefited from low interest rates, institutional adoption, and abundant liquidity. Hence, a new stimulus program could encourage retail investors to allocate more money toward Bitcoin and other risk assets.

However, the proposed dividend is not approved, and higher inflation expectations or Treasury yields could offset some of the bullish impact. If Democrats win control of Congress, Trump’s proposal could face a much tougher path toward approval.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

The Midterm election could also determine whether lawmakers make progress on the most-awaited crypto regulation, the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act. It aims to establish clearer rules governing digital assets and the division of responsibilities between US regulators.

The bill remains stalled after failing to advance through a Senate procedural vote in September. A Republican victory could improve its chances, although bipartisan support would still be necessary to overcome legislative hurdles.

A Democratic victory, particularly if the party takes control of the House, could bring increased scrutiny of Trump’s crypto-related ventures and campaign connections. That could delay legislation as lawmakers focus on investigations and oversight.

Still, a Democratic win would not automatically mean tougher crypto regulation. Bipartisan support for clearer digital asset rules remains possible, although the final legislation could look different from the current proposal.

The Midterm election presents a mixed outlook for crypto. A Republican victory combined with stimulus optimism, progress on crypto legislation, and Iran de-escalation would create a potentially bullish environment.

A Democratic victory could introduce regulatory uncertainty, while renewed conflict in the Middle East could pressure crypto regardless of the midterm election result. For us, the key question is whether political optimism can outweigh geopolitical risk.

Trump’s stimulus promise may offer a powerful bullish narrative, but crypto’s next major move could ultimately depend on improving liquidity or another inflationary shock.

The biggest immediate threat to crypto is not the midterm election, and it may come from outside Washington. The US carried out limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm islands near the Strait of Hormuz. This revived concerns about escalation, even as diplomatic contacts continued.

If you’re bullish on Bitcoin (BTC), you probably aren’t as bullish as Sam Altman’s OpenAI bot. ChatGPT AI predicts a potentially historic run for Bitcoin. It says a monster move may be on the cards if a hypothetical landmark catalyst hits the leading digital asset.

The concept revolves around a coordinated shift in the global insurance and pension industries. In this scenario, major industry bodies and regulators would formally endorse or require a modest allocation of Bitcoin as a permanent part of investment portfolios for diversification and as a hedge against inflation.

This framework would drive systematic purchasing by some of the world’s largest long-term capital pools, creating consistent structural demand for Bitcoin. As a result, this would significantly accelerate Bitcoin’s integration into traditional portfolio construction on an unprecedented scale.

On the higher timeframes, Bitcoin has been consolidating in the $77,000–$79,000 region after recent volatility. Price continues to defend key intermediate supports while facing resistance around the $82,000–$85,000 zone.

In a standard bull market, a sustained breakout above $90,000–$95,000 would confirm intermediate strength and open the path toward a retest of the prior all-time high near $110,000–$126,000.

Under the extreme insurance and pension allocation scenario outlined above, clearing that previous high would likely trigger powerful measured-move extensions and multi-cycle Fibonacci projections from the multi-year base.

Momentum indicators currently sit in neutral-to-corrective territory with substantial room to run into the extreme overbought readings characteristic of parabolic advances.

Key nearer-term supports sit near $76,000–$77,000 and $72,000–$74,000; holding those levels would keep the broader recovery structure intact.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei says security in the Strait of Hormuz could be restored and negotiations with the US could begin within days if Washington meets Tehran's demands under a revised seven-step plan. pic.twitter.com/XWEXMOzBxE

Several external developments could enhance this optimistic scenario. Globally, a lasting resolution to major geopolitical conflict, such as the Russia-Ukraine war or a permanent ceasefire involving Iran, along with the normalization of the Strait of Hormuz, could lower risk premiums and encourage capital to flow back into growth and alternative assets.

From an economic perspective, a clear shift by major central banks toward more accommodative monetary policy, coupled with elevated liquidity and concerns about the long-term purchasing power of fiat currencies, would boost demand for scarce digital assets.

Within the cryptocurrency space, continued growth in spot Bitcoin ETF inflows, broader institutional adoption, increasing corporate treasury allocations, and a sustained resurgence of risk appetite for digital assets would create a highly favorable liquidity environment, reinforcing Bitcoin’s status as the market’s primary reserve asset.

Under this highly speculative scenario, and assuming a full-blown crypto bull market returns alongside supportive external conditions, Bitcoin could reach between $850,000 and $1,500,000, with a stretch target toward $2,500,000+ by January 1, 2027.

This remains pure speculation and entertainment, not a realistic base-case outlook. The catalyst would require extraordinary coordination across the global insurance and pension industries that is currently highly unlikely.

#5374. Dogecoin Alert: Critical Wallet Security Threat Uncovered, What's Next?

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The Dogecoin community gets a security alert after wallet provider Trezor revealed a suspected hardware implant in its Safe 5 device bought from CryptoBilis.

Dogecoin community member Mishaboar urged users who purchased a Trezor device from CryptoBilis in March this year or later to take immediate precautions, including moving their funds to a completely new wallet with a freshly generated recovery seed.

"If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible," Mishaboar wrote.

If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible. Use a device and wallet you trust to create the new wallet. If your wallet supports an additional passphrase, use it (and remember to write it down in your offline backups). NEVER reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does NOT make your funds safe. An ELI5: I know this is obvious to many of you, but in my experience some people don't realize that hardware wallets don't actually "contain" their coins. Your coins "live" on the blockchain. Your wallet only holds the keys that allow you to access and spend them. If someone else has a copy of those keys, they can access your funds from anywhere in the world, from any device where those keys are imported. They don't need your physical little device or your phone to access it.

Users are warned never to reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does not make funds safe either.

Mishaboar highlighted a critical security principle that may not seem obvious to all users: hardware wallets do not actually "contain" coins—the coins "live" on the blockchain. The wallet only holds the keys that allow access to and spending of the coins. If someone obtains these keys, they can access the funds from anywhere in the world on any device where the keys are imported, without needing the physical device or the user's phone.

Mishaboar's warning follows a recent update from Trezor regarding CryptoBilis, in which the company disclosed that it had been alerted through responsible disclosure to a suspected hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device purchased from CryptoBilis in August 2026.

According to Trezor, the reported device has not yet been received for physical examination. However, the company said it considers the report credible enough to notify customers while its security team investigates. No CryptoBilis buyer has reported losing funds to the company so far.

In light of this, affected users are urged to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Those who have not yet set up their device should never do so using an existing wallet backup (recovery phrase), nor share this information with anyone.

Bitcoin (BTC) traded near $76,900 on Tuesday, November 3, as Americans voted in midterms that Polymarket traders see Democrats sweeping, 76.5% for the Senate and 94.5% for the House, a result that could push crypto’s market structure law to 2027 or later.

The industry spent big to stop that. Crypto-linked groups have put more than $200 million into this cycle. Yet the bill they most wanted, the CLARITY Act, is still stuck in the Senate, seven weeks after a 49-50 vote left it 11 votes short.

Now the clock is the problem. Any bill that hasn’t passed when this Congress ends on January 3 dies with it, and the next Congress would have to start from scratch.

BTC USD price itself is down 1.3% in 24 hours and 9.8% over the past month, and it is sitting right on its 200-day average. Spot ETFs lost $398.6 million on Monday, and the Fear & Greed Index reads 26.

So how long could a Democratic Congress hold up crypto laws, and does the market care?

One law is done, the other is stalled. The GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law, was signed in July 2025, and Treasury says its rules are on track. The CLARITY Act never made it through the Senate. It would decide when a token falls under the SEC or the CFTC.

The House passed it 294-134 on July 17, 2025. The Senate Banking Committee advanced its version 15-9 in May. Then, on September 15, a vote to open debate failed 49-50 when it needed 60.

Almost certainly for this bill. Democrats need a net gain of four seats for the Senate, and prediction market traders gave them a 74% chance on Monday, the highest since the market opened.

The only route left for the current text is the lame duck session between the election and January. NYDIG’s Greg Cipolaro said in May that it works only if Republicans keep the Senate and Majority Leader John Thune puts it ahead of government funding deadlines. If Democrats win, he said, the bill is unlikely to move when the new Congress starts.

The White House isn’t counting on it either. “There’s no holding them back in hopes of a lame duck passage of the bill,” crypto adviser Patrick Witt said in September, pointing the SEC and CFTC to write rules on their own.

A Democratic Senate would also hand the gavels to people who voted against this bill. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Banking Committee, opposed it in May and would be in line to chair it. Expect a new draft with:

Then there is the White House. President Trump has already said that if Democrats win the House, “I guess I’ll become Mr Veto.” A bill both sides can pass, and he will sign, means starting over in 2027.

"I guess I'll become Mr. Veto."President Trump lays out his strategy for dealing with a potential Democratic-controlled Congress in an exclusive interview with Miranda Devine.Trump says he would veto legislation before eventually negotiating compromises, while expressing hope… pic.twitter.com/n63QdC5MV0

Former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, now on OKX’s board, called it “a hostile Congress” for the industry. Still, not everything stops: regulators’ rules don’t need a vote, though without a law behind them, they are easier to challenge in court and to reverse under the next president.

Barely. BTC trades at $76,903, just above the 200-day EMA at $76,504, and 39% below its $126,080 record from October 2025.

A Democratic sweep is mostly priced in. The surprise would be a Republican Senate, which would reopen the lame duck window for the CLARITY Act.

#5371. Bitcoin Turns 18: Satoshi's Whitepaper Anniversary Marks Crypto Milestone

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. It's the 18th anniversary of the Bitcoin whitepaper. Today marks the historic date on which its pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto published the blueprint for the first digital cash.

On Oct. 31, 2008, a nine-page white paper called "Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System" was published, laying out a radical vision for transferring value electronically without the need for conventional financial intermediaries.

Bitcoin supporters, exchanges, and the rest of the crypto community are filling social media platform X with celebratory wishes on the 18th anniversary of Bitcoin's unveiling to the world.

Bitcoin proponent and Strategy Chairman Michael Saylor wrote on X: "Happy Bitcoin white paper day. 18 years."

One of the most salient features of the whitepaper is the fixed supply of Bitcoin at 21 million coins. The pre-determined issuance structure is what makes Bitcoin different from traditional monetary systems, where central authorities can inflate the money supply.

Major U.S. crypto exchange Coinbase highlighted this fact in its X post: "21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day. https://t.co/JtKeHtCuSM

"Today marks 18 years since the release of the Bitcoin Whitepaper. A day that changed everything," Coinbase continued.

Stablecoin issuer Tether wrote: "On 31 October 2008, Satoshi published nine pages that explained Bitcoin to the world. Today we're explaining it to everyone else. Two pizzas, 10,000 BTC, 21 million coins, and one key you never share. Everything you need to know, in a comic. Happy 18th birthday, Bitcoin whitepaper."

Crypto platform Uphold wrote: "Nine pages that challenged the entire legacy financial system. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

The Bitcoin whitepaper laid the groundwork for the network's launch in January 2009, when Satoshi Nakamoto mined Bitcoin's genesis block and introduced the first units of the cryptocurrency.

When Bitcoin launched on January 3, 2009, it had no market value or official exchange price. Over the years, Bitcoin has evolved from a niche technological experiment into a globally recognized digital asset. Its emergence has influenced the development of thousands of cryptocurrencies, blockchain applications, and decentralized financial systems.

The cryptocurrency now trades at $77,310 and is worth $1.55 trillion, according to CoinMarketCap data.

The world's largest meme token by market capitalization is headed towards concluding the month with another massive loss, just like it did last year.

While this is marking the second consecutive year Dogecoin would record a loss for the widely-praised month, the asset has extended the negative trend recorded in October 2024.

Historical data showcased by CryptoRank shows that DOGE has posted a negative return of 20.1% this October, after it recorded a 20% loss in the same month last year.

While this shows that the asset has performed the same way in both years, the data has drawn attention from market participants as the decline has come despite the massive optimism surrounding October, a month traditionally recognized as a strong month for all major cryptocurrencies.

In addition to the extended Uptober failure, the decline recorded this month has broken the two-month streak of consistent gains posted in August and September, marking a sudden flip in market sentiment.

With the October loss already representing a weak start to the last quarter of the year, it remains uncertain if Dogecoin will be able to pick up pace in the remaining two months and close the year on a stronger note.

XRP's burn rate is shooting up toward the end of October, surging 147%. According to data from XRPScan, XRP burned as fees came in at 1,644 on October 30.

The burn activity is a representation of the XRP Ledger's deflationary mechanism, which permanently removes small amounts of XRP from circulation every time transactions are processed on the network.

Some blockchains have scheduled mechanisms to distribute burned tokens, but XRP burns are automatic through transaction fees. Every transaction on the XRP Ledger requires a fee denominated in XRP and that fee is burned.

A total of 14,423,678 XRP, representing 0.014% of its total supply, has been burned so far.

Often referred to as "Uptober" in crypto circles thanks to a track record of outperformance, October might need to shed that nickname given that major cryptocurrencies, including XRP, are down for the month. With few hours left in the month, XRP is down 15.86% so far, on track for its first red month since July.

XRP closed August and September up 30.11% and 7.91% respectively, with traders expecting the positive price run to continue, but this was not to be, as concerns within and outside the market weighed on crypto markets.

The most recent is the Binance heist, which saw $6.3 billion in client assets stolen. In a positive update, Binance said it has covered about 90% of the value of cryptocurrency that hackers stole earlier this week and plans to restore withdrawals by Sunday, making progress on a pledge to fully reimburse customers.

XRP had a nice Q3 2026 and the official XRP X account shared key highlights. The amount of stablecoins on the XRP Ledger increased by 25.2% to $1.03 billion, while net inflows of XRP ETP globally jumped by 39.6% to $355.3 million. Payment volume rose 4.3% to 42.82 billion XRP, while native DEX volume rose 20.2% to $614.8 million. Distributed tokenized RWA value jumped 29.2% to $498.7 million as Aviva's investors launched a tokenized fund with BNY Mellon.

Devcon attendees got an unexpected laugh when Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin appeared on stage wearing a green cloak and a smiling mask. The unusual cosplay stole the spotlight as Bitmine ETH accumulation continued, with the company adding another 8,573 Ethereum to its massive treasury.

Buterin’s costume looked more suited to a fantasy game than one of crypto’s biggest developer gatherings. The playful Vitalik appearance offered a lighter moment at Devcon 8 in Mumbai, where developers and researchers are discussing Ethereum’s future.

Meanwhile, Bitmine Immersion Technologies is pursuing a much more serious mission: accumulating enough ETH to control 5% of its total supply. The company’s latest disclosure showed holdings of 6,060,506 ETH as of November 1, worth $13.7 billion at its current price of $2,261. Bitmine now controls around 4.9% of Ethereum’s supply, putting it close to its ambitious accumulation target.

Discover: The Crypto Presales This Q4 2026

Devcon 8 runs from November 3 to November 6 in Mumbai, bringing Ethereum developers, researchers, and ecosystem participants together for four days of talks and workshops. But Buterin’s unusual outfit delivered an unexpected highlight during the event.

The Vitalik Devcon appearance showed the lighter side of Ethereum’s culture, even as the network faces serious questions about adoption, scaling, and ETH’s market performance.

@VitalikButerin just opened Devcon and set the tone for the week.A formally verified OS, open silicon, self-sovereign healthtech, free discourse, private communication, trustworthy AI — these are all part of Ethereum's mission. https://t.co/51UfMsxk5o pic.twitter.com/TynzSuzmhX

Bitmine, however, appears unfazed by the market uncertainty. The company purchased 8,573 ETH during the latest reported week, worth roughly $19.4 million at its disclosed valuation. Its total crypto, cash, and other investments reached $14.5 billion, including 216 BTC and $498 million in cash and marketable securities.

🧵1/BitMine provided its latest holdings update for November 2, 2026$14.5 billion in total crypto + "moonshots":– 6,060,506 ETH at $2,261per ETH (per @coinbase)– 216 Bitcoin (BTC)– $180 million stake in Beast Industries @MrBeast– $82 million stake in Eightco Holdings…

Bitmine has also staked 5.23 million ETH, representing 86% of its holdings. The company estimates that its current staking position could generate around $358 million in annualized rewards, potentially rising to $415 million if its entire ETH treasury were staked.

That creates a second part of its Ethereum thesis. Accumulating the asset while generating yield from the network.

Ethereum’s bullish outlook rests on more than Bitmine’s buying activity. Staking removes ETH from immediate trading circulation, while institutional treasury accumulation can add another source of demand. Bitmine’s holdings alone now represent nearly one in every 20 ETH in existence.

The company’s growing staking position also shows Ethereum’s proof-of-stake model, where holders can earn rewards by helping secure the network. Bitmine’s projected staking income gives it an incentive to maintain its ETH exposure rather than simply trade around short-term price moves.

Price forecasts remain ambitious. Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee has suggested Ethereum could revisit its previous all-time high near $4,954 before the end of 2026, with $6,000 also emerging as a potential year-end target.

At $2,261, ETH would need to climb 119% to reach $4,954 and around 165% to hit $6,000. The technical picture still needs improvement. Ethereum faces resistance around the $2,315 area, identified as a key moving-average level in recent market analysis.

A sustained move above that zone could strengthen the recovery case, while a failure to reclaim it would leave ETH vulnerable to further downside.

There are risks to the bullish thesis. U.S. spot Ethereum ETFs recorded substantial outflows during October, while ETH’s price performance remained under pressure. Institutional accumulation has not yet translated into a decisive market reversal.

Still, Bitmine’s continued buying, its massive staked position, and Ethereum’s potential price recovery are keeping long-term bulls engaged.

Vitalik and his Devcon cosplay may have provided the conference’s funniest moment, but Bitmine’s growing treasury is the more serious signal. If institutional demand returns and ETH breaks through key resistance, $6,000 could move back into the conversation.

#5364. Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Daily pool data shows Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

ZecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

Across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

The deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable."

The coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

As of ZecStats' latest update on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

In October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who plan to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

In practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Users need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

The useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

#5363. Binance to Resume XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum and Other Crypto Withdrawals

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance will allow withdrawals for major cryptocurrencies such as XRP, Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL), among others, after suspending withdrawals because of a massive security breach involving $6.3 billion.

Binance announced on Nov. 1 that the exchange would begin resuming withdrawal services between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC.

Binance emphasized that the withdrawal resumption process will be carried out progressively as the exchange conducts security and infrastructure readiness checks.

"We aim to restore withdrawals progressively as we complete security and readiness checks," said Binance.

Binance continued to offer deposit services during the security breach.

The first phase of withdrawal resumption will include a total of 15 blockchain networks.

This list includes popular networks such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Ledger, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Tron, and Dogecoin.

Other cryptocurrencies that will be available for withdrawals include Zcash (ZEC), Avalanche (AVAX), Sui (SUI), Polygon (POL) and Arbitrum (ARB).

Withdrawals of major stablecoins such as Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) will also be enabled on multiple networks.

The exchange noted that it selected the assets based on user withdrawal demand over the past week.

The exchange also warned that not all listed cryptocurrencies and networks may be enabled at the same time.

The withdrawal resumption comes only days after Binance suffered a massive security breach.

The breach led to the theft of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from the exchange's hot wallets.

The exchange temporarily paused withdrawals in order to contain the damage, conduct an investigation into the security breach and avoid additional losses.

Binance has now disclosed that it has recovered around 95% of affected assets.

This is up from 90% when Binance last provided an update on the recovery process.

The exchange said that it has fully backed the balances of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, BNB, USDT, USDC, Zcash, USD1, and Ripple USD (RLUSD).

The remaining 5% includes cryptocurrencies that are less liquid and harder to buy in large amounts.

#5361. Do Not Use Your iPhone as Hardware Wallet, OneKey Founder

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Using an old iPhone as a crypto cold wallet may be less safe than it looks, OneKey founder Yishi Wang has warned. The practice is popular with self-custody fans: wipe a spare phone, take it offline, and keep your wallet recovery information on it.

Wang's worry is that an offline phone can still be attacked by someone who has it in their hands. He has pointed to flaws in several generations of iPhone. These include the publicly documented checkm8 issue on older models and, more recently reported, low-level weaknesses in certain later devices. They sit in the early stages of the boot process. A malicious app isn't involved.

An iOS update may not fix a weakness built into immutable boot code. Switching off Wi-Fi and cellular does nothing about someone who gets physical access to the phone. A vulnerability still doesn't automatically mean an attacker can recover a seed phrase, though. Device encryption, passcode strength and secure key handling remain real barriers.

Wang advises against trusting iPhone 11-generation and older devices with recovery phrases. If you think a phrase may have been exposed, create a completely new one using a trusted setup and move your funds to that wallet. Generating another address from the same seed won't help, because the underlying exposure stays.

He also stresses updated operating systems, long alphanumeric passcodes and careful control of USB connections. Earlier, he suggested that even newer iPhones shouldn't be treated as equivalent to purpose-built signing devices when the holdings are substantial and long-term.

Dedicated hardware wallets are built to isolate signing keys and let you check transaction details on the device itself. They carry risk too. Counterfeit hardware, compromised distribution channels and sloppy recovery-phrase handling can all undermine their security.

The argument is about threat models, not brand loyalty. An offline phone cuts remote exposure, but that doesn't turn it into a secure hardware wallet.

#5359. Circle Begins CCTP V1 Wind-Down Amid Doc Mismatch

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

Circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

Most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

Embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It says: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

The schedule is fixed. Circle announced in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026."

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide says "message limits will tighten over time until no new burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the company wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible."

Funds already in transit are protected. The guide says "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations."

The migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1."

The main text above it says something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:

Circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

As of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle said "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Many developers now ask AI assistants to write or update integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

The fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

For teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

For Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

For everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

Ripple's scheduled November escrow unlock has put 1 billion XRP into circulation, with blockchain data tracker Whale Alert reporting two transactions in this regard.

According to Whale Alert, 500,000,000 XRP (626,430,089 USD) was unlocked at Ripple in the early hours of November 1; another 500,000,000 XRP (626,430,089 USD) was unlocked, bringing the total unlock to 1 billion XRP tokens.

🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 🔓 500,000,000 $XRP (626,430,089 USD) unlocked at #Ripple https://t.co/ejC9qFmsjb

Ripple's monthly unlocks are part of the firm's ongoing process to increase transparency and predictability around XRP distribution. The company initially put 55 billion XRP in escrow and released it in an organized fashion over time to manage the supply of XRP entering circulation.

But not all of the 1 billion XRP that was released stays on the market. In the past, Ripple has returned a large portion of the unlocked XRP (about 700 million XRP) to escrow while keeping some of it to facilitate operational needs, liquidity, and ecosystem-related activities.

October was a big month for Ripple and the XRP ecosystem, as it saw a slew of announcements and updates for the XRP Ledger. It also hosted two of the largest events for XRP and Ripple: Swell and the XRP Seoul events.

RLUSD was listed on Coinbase in October, allowing retail and institutional clients to trade and manage RLUSD through Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange, and the Coinbase Retail app, with 1:1 conversion from U.S. dollars and other supported USD-denominated stablecoins into RLUSD.

The XRP Ledger is set for crucial fixes and improvements over the next few days. According to XRPScan data, fixCleanup3_4_0, which began its two-week activation window on Oct 21, 2026, after a reset in voting, now eyes the earliest activation date being 2:46 PM UTC on Nov 4, 2026.

Validator support for the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment must stay above 80% for it to activate. If it slips to 80% or lower even once, the amendment is rejected and the 14-day timer starts over.

This fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment is a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment is essential for Permission Delegation, which went live in October, as until it is enabled, users would not be able to delegate the PaymentBurn granular permission.
