Binance has published its latest Proof of Reserves report as of October 31, 2026. Judging by it, client funds are still fully backed — despite the largest hack in crypto history at the end of the month. Coverage for XRP is 100.99%, and for the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin, 100.83%.

A comparison of balances as of October 1 and October 31 shows how the exchange's liabilities and reserves changed after the October 29 attack: hackers then withdrew about $6.3 billion from its wallets across ten blockchains.

Immediately after the attack, Binance suspended withdrawals and deposits, so the growth of balances in Ripple assets occurred before the hack. October results:

The main thing in the report is something else: Binance confirmed full coverage of the ten most traded assets, including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB and SOL — and did so just two days after the hack.

About $3 billion of the stolen funds was quickly frozen directly on the blockchains with the help of partners, including Tether, Circle and Ripple. To cover the losses and return reserves to 1:1, Binance allocated more than $6.34 billion of its own capital. This reserve included the SAFU fund, the Binance Futures insurance fund and retained earnings.

The remaining 5% of losses are in low-liquidity tokens: they are being quietly bought back through over-the-counter (OTC) desks so as not to crash spot prices.

Each client can verify their own balance: the report is built on Merkle trees and zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs). For the market, this case sets a new bar: an exchange is no longer judged by whether it gets hacked, but by how quickly it stops an attack and whether it has enough of its own money to plug the hole.

Attackers reportedly compromised three Binance engineers before reaching the internal wallet signing service.

The timeline spans June, September and October, involving tampered software and a malicious code repository.

A claim blaming a Google ad has not been established by the preliminary investigation.

A major Binance hack didn’t begin with some sophisticated attack on the exchange’s front door. According to a preliminary investigation timeline, attackers compromised employees, stole credentials and eventually reached the platform’s internal wallet signing service.

The sequence raises uncomfortable questions about internal security. Three engineers became part of an attack chain that ultimately enabled unauthorized asset transfers.

The trouble reportedly started in June, when Wallet DevOps Engineer A downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer while configuring an AI coding tool. Binance detected the incident, replaced the device and rotated credentials. However, information about the engineer and colleagues had already been exposed.

Then came September. Engineer B downloaded a malicious code repository during what appeared to be a fake job interview, compromising his work computer.

Binance Hack Timeline: How Attackers Compromised Three Engineers to Access Wallet Signing ServiceWuBlockchain mapped the attack timeline based on Binance’s preliminary investigation. In June, Wallet DevOps Engineer A downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer while setting up an… pic.twitter.com/laEv7JMLBS

On October 20, attackers reportedly used the compromised device and an internal AI tool to gain control over Engineers A and C. They also discovered a container deployment permission token on Engineer A’s computer.

The operation escalated on October 29. Attackers accessed Engineer C’s device, used credentials stolen from A, deployed a container and executed a malicious script. That sequence ultimately enabled unauthorized transfers through Binance’s internal wallet signing service.

A separate commentator claimed the roughly $6 billion Binance hack resulted from a developer clicking a malicious Google advertisement, and argued Google should be held responsible.

However, the preliminary timeline does not establish that connection. It describes a tampered installer and a malicious repository, not a confirmed Google ad as the entry point.

Wow, turns out the $6 billion Binance hack was caused by a Binance developer clicking a malicious Google ad!I maintain my position: it's more important than ever to hold Google liable for platforming scams and turning a blind eye.Google was complicit in the Binance hack. https://t.co/RZwzjzdT9L pic.twitter.com/GhnFAQB1LM

The distinction matters. The Binance hack timeline points to compromised engineers, exposed credentials and deployment permissions as key parts of the attack. Blaming an advertising platform without evidence risks obscuring the specific security failures investigators are still examining.

#5306. Solana Officially Scores 1,000 Days Without Outage

The Solana network has hit a significant milestone in its quest to overcome its early hurdles, successfully going 1,000 days without a network-wide outage.

This feat stands in stark contrast to Solana's past, when the blockchain experienced some notable network disruptions. One of the more significant outages occurred in September 2021, when a spike in bot traffic from Grape Protocol IDO transactions led to a surge in transactions that overwhelmed validators and hindered consensus, resulting in a roughly 17-hour network outage.

The Solana network experienced similar problems in April 2022, with a large traffic spike due to an NFT mint that led to a roughly 7-hour outage. Another outage happened in June 2022, when a bug involving durable nonce transactions caused block production to stop for roughly 4.5 hours. Finally, in September 2022, the network experienced a fork due to a bug in the consensus layer, which led to a halt in block production lasting over 6 hours.

The final major outage occurred back in February 2023, when abnormal block forwarding overwhelmed Solana's Turbine block propagation system, leaving validators stuck in a vote-only state and leading to a coordinated restart. This would prove to be a monumental event for Solana in terms of its engineering progress.

Solana has seen a string of updates and engineering innovations by its developers in an effort to improve the network's ability to avoid the failures that had plagued it in the past. Some of these features include stake-weighted quality of service to better prioritize traffic from staked validators. The network also saw networking innovations such as QUIC that provide more flexibility in dealing with spam and congestion. There have also been updates to deduplication logic following the February 2023 outage. Additionally, the network has seen innovations such as a local fee market and other scheduling improvements to discourage users and bots from spamming the network with duplicate transactions.

Recently, Solana has emphasized that network resilience should be taken seriously. In a September 2026 update, the project shared that the network has seen 100% uptime since February 2024 and has continued to handle large amounts of traffic. It also highlighted a major infrastructure provider experiencing a routing failure in August 2026 that caused validators representing nearly 29% of the network's stake to go offline, but this did not result in a halt in block production. The project uses this as an example of increased fault tolerance.

For Solana, this 1,000-day milestone is not just a success in terms of network uptime. It's a statement and a demonstration to the world that a network once mocked for outages can now support serious financial and on-chain use cases.

Results of the 2026 US midterm elections will start coming in once the first polls close at 6pm Eastern Time on Tuesday, or 4:30am IST on Wednesday, beginning with parts of Indiana and Kentucky. Most of Florida, Georgia and Virginia close at 7pm ET (5:30am IST), and Pennsylvania, Maine and most of Michigan and Texas at 8pm ET (6:30am IST). Arizona, Iowa, Minnesota and Wisconsin close at 9pm ET (7:30am IST), California at 11pm ET (9:30am IST), and the last polls in western Alaska at 1am ET (11:30am IST). Early tallies are not final, because outlets such as the Associated Press call a race only when the margin is clear. Mail ballots and ranked-choice counting in Alaska, Maine, California, Nevada and Arizona could delay close races by days, so control of Congress may not be known on election night.

#5302. BNB Crypto Drops 8.7% in an Hour as Binance Loses $6.36 Billion to Hackers, and Futures Traders Turn Short: Can BNB Hold Its 200-Day Average?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour after the Binance hack and is lagging Bitcoin, as shorts pile in. Can BNB hold its 200-day EMA at $692?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour on Thursday, October 29, from $744.90 to $680, as hackers drained about $6.36 billion from Binance, the exchange behind the token, in the largest crypto theft on record. The bounce since has been the weakest among the big coins. BNB trades at $702, down 6.2% in 24 hours, with a $92.4 billion market cap and 48.7% below its $1,370 record from October 2025. In futures, traders who bet against it are now paying to keep those bets open.

So why is BNB taking the hack harder than Bitcoin, what happened to it after Binance’s last two security scares, and where are the levels that matter?

If a $6.3B security breach can't completely break $BNB, what will?

The market is testing @BNBCHAIN resilience right now.

Historically, moments of maximum fear can create the best opportunities.

DISCOVER: Meme coin supercycle: Top performers this week

Because it is the coin most tied to Binance itself, and futures traders are now betting on that link. From the 20:00 UTC price on Thursday, BNB is still down 5.6%, more than Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP or Dogecoin.

Large-cap coins since the Binance hack. Source: Binance

The hack itself didn’t touch BNB Chain. TRM Labs’ breakdown lists ten blockchains the attacker drained Binance wallets on, from Ethereum to Polygon, and BNB Chain isn’t among them. What traders are pricing is the exchange: BNB is Binance’s token, so a hit to Binance reads as a hit to BNB.

“The Binance exploit has intensified market-wide selling, with BNB facing the greatest exposure,” Zeus Research analyst Dominick John said. Rick Maeda of Laevitas saw it the other way, calling the drop “quite modest for possibly the largest exchange theft ever.”

The futures market sides with the bears. On OKX:

Put together, that reads as many small accounts buying the dip and fewer, larger traders shorting it. If BNB bounces, those shorts are fuel for a squeeze. If it breaks lower, the crowded longs are.

It fell further at first, then recovered within a month both times. Binance has been here twice before:

This time BNB is 8.7% under its pre-hack price at its worst so far. If it follows either path, there could be another leg down before any recovery.

The comparison traders keep reaching for is FTT, the FTX token that lost almost all its value when the exchange collapsed in November 2022. The difference is the balance sheet. FTX had spent customer money and couldn’t pay it back. Binance says it will cover all losses from this hack, and Tether, Circle and others froze about $2.7 billion of the stolen funds within hours.

Traders haven’t fully relaxed, though. Binance hasn’t said how it will fund the payout, and withdrawals stay shut until the reopening it expects within 48 hours of its Friday morning update.

EXPLORE: CZ Tells Crypto Users to Be “Extra Careful” Online as PHP Vulnerabilities Hit the Code Behind 70% of Websites: Can a Hacked Site Drain Your Wallet?

It is holding by a thin margin. BNB closed Thursday at $698.46, just above its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $692.46, after the hack-hour wick to $680 dipped below it. The 50-day EMA at $733.06 is now overhead.

The four-month chart puts BNB back where it was in late August. It traded between $674.60 and $726 for two weeks before breaking out in early September and running to $809.99 on October 5. Thursday’s drop erased that whole move.

For BNB crypto, the next 48 hours carry more weight than any chart line. A smooth reopening of Binance withdrawals would leave the shorts on the wrong side of a crowded trade. A delay, or any sign Binance is selling BNB to pay for the hack, would put $674.60 in play.

Brazilian crypto platform Mercado Bitcoin has confirmed the detection and containment of an issue in one of its systems. As a precaution, the exchange has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, assuring clients of the safety of their assets and the absence of a data leak.

The incident occurred shortly after the platform passed a local licensing deadline.

According to independent blockchain company Hypernative, suspicious outflows from wallets linked to the exchange exceeded $40 million (approximately 217 million reais). Analysts recorded the movement of assets on the Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana, Tron and Stellar (XLM) networks.

In total, the activity spanned at least 10 blockchains, also including Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche and BNB Smart Chain. The first suspicious transfers were recorded at around 02:15 UTC and involved Bitcoin deposit addresses attributed to the exchange.

Among the flagged assets were 106 BTC and 2,852 ETH. The hackers carried out direct token transfers, which indicates a compromise of operational reserves rather than segregated client assets.

Among the withdrawn assets, blockchain analysts recorded a large volume of Stellar tokens: about 6.7 million XLM were consolidated at addresses linked to the suspicious transactions.

As part of the investigation and coordination of efforts with the authorities, Mercado Bitcoin published a specific Stellar destination address to help the community and security firms track the movement of assets in real time.

The move is aimed at monitoring the movement of tokens and preventing their laundering through third-party services.

At the moment, the exchange is conducting an investigation, tracking the assets and promising to provide regular updates. The exchange has not yet confirmed the amount involved, disclosed which system was compromised or given a date for resuming deposits and withdrawals.

Until the platform fully resumes normal operations and the security of its infrastructure is confirmed, users are advised to refrain from making new deposits.

Leading Brazilian cryptocurrency exchange and Ripple blockchain payments partner Mercado Bitcoin has announced a temporary freeze on cryptocurrency deposits and withdrawals after acknowledging a security breach.

As the firm revealed in an official announcement, the security breach did not cause any harm to its users or compromise their personal data.

Mercado Bitcoin stressed that the incident did not harm any customers or lead to a data breach.

Nevertheless, as a precautionary measure, the firm decided to temporarily halt deposits and withdrawals while its security teams conduct further investigations into the issue and try to locate any assets that could have been affected.

Additionally, Mercado Bitcoin said that it is working with the appropriate authorities to investigate the incident.

“We are still working to safely restore operations and will keep our customers updated on our official channels,” the exchange announced.

Interestingly, the company also released some cryptocurrency wallet addresses related to suspicious transactions linked to the incident.

The move aims to assist blockchain investigators and other industry players in keeping track of possibly compromised assets on different networks.

#5297. Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying, as Route 2 FI Buys the Dip

Bitcoin news: the Binance hacker holds $1.4B in BTC, 3x this week’s ETF inflows. Will Binance’s buyback help, and can BTC hold $76,500?

Bitcoin news on Friday turned to a warning from trader Route 2 FI, who said the Binance hacker’s $1.4 billion in BTC is more than three times what spot ETFs bought all week, a potential seller hanging over Bitcoin at $77,300.

Arkham’s entity page shows the Binance hacker holding 18,270 BTC worth $1.42 billion and 488,364 ETH worth $1.09 billion across 73 addresses. US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million from Monday to Thursday.

Route 2 FI still likes the setup enough to take a position. The trader expects Binance to recover fully but thinks the hack will push more people toward decentralized exchanges.

Binance would need a couple of months to fill this hole, unless they use other shady tactics to get whole faster.

The hacker has $BTC worth $1.4b and $ETH worth $1b ready to sell. For $BTC, that's more than 3x the $450M that spot ETFs bought all week.

— Route 2 FI (@Route2FI) October 30, 2026

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Holds $79,200 Before the Fed, Coinbase Earnings and a $10.9B Expiry: Which Way Next?

Route 2 FI’s math holds up. Arkham’s Binance Hacker entity shows 18,270 BTC, worth $1.42 billion at Friday’s prices. SoSoValue figures show US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million across four straight days of inflows from October 26 to 29. That makes the hacker’s Bitcoin about 3.2 times a week of ETF demand.

Binance hacker holdings on October 30, 2026 vs spot Bitcoin ETF inflows for October 26 to 29. Sources: Arkham, SoSoValue.

The hacker hasn’t sold any of the Bitcoin yet. The selling so far has been in smaller tokens: Lookonchain tracked the attacker dumping UNI, PEPE, ENA, LINK and others for 70,480 ETH, worth about $158 million.

On the other side, Binance is already buying. The exchange told CoinDesk it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover the losses, $5 billion of it already held in the same tokens the attackers took, and is buying the rest on exchanges and over the counter. About $3 billion of the stolen funds is frozen and doesn’t need replacing.

“Binance’s SAFU fund and Binance’s holdings include a large amount of assets such as BTC and ETH. We are currently buying, through OTC and on-exchange, all the stolen altcoins in fully matching amounts.”

That matters for Bitcoin. If Binance already holds enough BTC to cover customers, its buying lands mostly on altcoins, which leaves the hacker’s 18,270 BTC as a seller without a matching buyer.

Route 2 FI pointed to the Bybit hack as the template. Attackers took about $1.4 billion in ether from Bybit on February 21, 2025, and the exchange replaced it within days through loans, deposits and market purchases.

The buyback gave prices only a short lift. Measured from the February 20, 2025 close on Binance:

Ethereum bounced while Bybit bought, then lost more than a third of its value within three weeks. The broader market sold off over that stretch for reasons beyond the hack, so the table shows that buyback demand fades fast. It doesn’t show that the hack caused the slide.

Route 2 FI also argued that the hack, coming a year after the October 10, 2025 crash, gives traders another reason to keep less money on centralized exchanges. Binance paid out more than $283 million in compensation after that crash, when some assets lost their pegs on its platform.

The trader cited the jump in Hyperliquid’s HYPE token as proof. The timing doesn’t fit, though. HYPE rose from $79.38 to a $97.09 high between 10:00 and 16:00 UTC on Thursday, after ICE and Trade.xyz announced plans for a regulated US perpetuals venue on Hyperliquid. That was about ten hours before the Binance drain began at 20:04 UTC.

After the hack, HYPE fell to $88.55 and trades at $90.83.

The setup Route 2 FI is buying is easy to see on the daily chart since early August. Bitcoin’s $76,500 low on Friday stopped $35 above its 200-day EMA at $76,465, a line it has closed above every day since the late-August breakout. BTC trades at $77,326, down 3.5% in 24 hours.

August 2 to October 30, 2026: BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

The last time Bitcoin tested the 200-day line, in mid-September, it held at $74,968 and climbed to $87,395 within a week. A trader buying here has a clear line to be wrong at.

For Bitcoin news over the coming week, two things decide which row plays out: whether Binance reopens withdrawals on schedule, and whether the hacker’s Bitcoin starts to move.

OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) are facing growing opposition to their plan to bring US stocks onto blockchain networks. Six more companies, including Tesla, Amazon, SpaceX and Netflix, have objected to having their shares tokenized on the proposed platform.

Can OKX and ICE still launch their tokenized stock platform?

#5294. NEAR Intents Head Names 3 Survival Rules for Crypto Wallets

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. The end of October 2026 was marked by the largest incident in the history of the crypto market — the $6.3 billion hack of the Binance exchange. This case exposed the vulnerability of the instant exchange (swaps) infrastructure.

While the automated systems of the North Korean group TraderTraitor withdrew $242 million via the Tron blockchain in the first two days, decentralized bridges and liquidity aggregators de facto became the main tool for legalizing the stolen funds.

Against this backdrop, the head of NEAR Intents Alex Shevchenko issued a warning to cryptocurrency wallet developers. His position is pragmatic: focusing exclusively on finding the best rate for the user turns services into unwitting accomplices in cybercrimes.

Since around $3.5 billion still remains under the hackers’ control after a wave of emergency freezes, regulatory pressure on the Web3 sector will inevitably increase. To minimize risks, the head of NEAR Intents formulated three basic survival rules for modern crypto wallets when choosing integration partners:

For wallet developers, the problem is structural. A single swap often passes through several protocols at once — an aggregator, a bridge and multiple liquidity pools — and each hop dilutes responsibility.

If any link in this chain processes tainted funds, the wallet through which the transaction was initiated shares the reputational damage and, increasingly, the legal exposure.

This is why due diligence on integration partners is shifting from an optional step to a core product requirement.

Investments in compliance and integration security are no longer a boring formality. The market has reached a point where the reputational and legal cleanliness of a service is valued far higher than saving a few cents on fees.

#5291. Lisk Officially Shuts Down Blockchain After 10 Years

Long-standing blockchain project Lisk has officially ended its blockchain operations after 10 years of existence, moving on to a new financial platform for businesses.

Lisk announced on Nov. 2 the official shutdown of its blockchain after 10 years of existence. This marks the end of one of the longest-lived blockchains in the crypto world.

"Today, the Lisk Chain has officially shut down," the project said in an X post.

With the blockchain shutdown, Lisk has ended its Portal and Bridge services. The rest of the blockchain's infrastructure is also being powered down.

The blockchain shutdown marks a significant milestone in the evolution of the Lisk project, which was launched in 2016 and has seen several changes over the years.

The Lisk team, however, has noted that the shutdown of the blockchain does not spell the end of the Lisk project.

The company is transforming into a new financial platform, one that enables businesses to manage both traditional currencies and stablecoins in one place.

"For 10 years, Lisk built onchain with developers, stakers and holders that made Lisk what it is," Lisk said.

The Lisk project has made it clear that its native token, LSK, will continue to exist even as the blockchain closes shop.

According to the team, LSK will still exist on Ethereum as the loyalty token for its new business financial platform.

In addition, the project announced plans to burn approximately 5.23 million LSK tokens left in its staking rewards pool.

The total figure includes unallocated rewards to users as well as unclaimed earned rewards.

The LSK tokens are set to be burned, permanently removing them from circulation. This will also lower the overall supply of the cryptocurrency.

This comes after a large burn of LSK tokens in September. At the time, Lisk burned 100 million LSK tokens after making the decision to wind down its decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) through a governance vote.

The burn event reduced the LSK token's supply from 400 million to 300 million LSK.

Lisk intends to introduce new use cases for LSK in 2027. This will allow businesses to earn rewards in the token and use LSK for platform fees.

#5290. FBI blames North Korea for the $6.3B Binance hack – Kim Yo Jong slams back

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The $6.3 billion Binance hack has drawn international attention after the FBI blames North Korea as responsible for the 29th October theft.

The agency attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a state-sponsored hacking group. Kim Yo Jong, Kim Jong-un’s sister, accused the United States of using fabrications to create the U.S. accusations against North Korea for its alleged theft.

This latest development has taken the focus off the hack itself, putting the spotlight back onto the issue of who was responsible for it.

The FBI is also examining blockchain links to previous hacks, including the $1.5 billion Bybit attack, to verify its suspicions.

As a result of this possible rift in the investigation process, recovery of stolen assets, along with establishing accountability, will likely be even more complicated.

Beyond the diplomatic dispute, the movement of the stolen funds provides another way to assess the FBI’s attribution. Blockchain analytics firms have traced the assets across 12,000 wallets and more than 40,000 transactions on 11 blockchains.

Furthermore, according to blockchain analytics firms, many of the Binance proceeds have been laundered through TRON [TRX]. This is by rapidly transferring funds between various addresses, repeatedly cycling the funds through various addresses.

Other methods used in the laundering process include cross-chain bridges, DeFi swaps, and very little usage of mixers. These connections can provide insight to investigators as to what might constitute a common network among hackers conducting similar hacks.

However, tracking movement of funds does allow investigators to see how funds were laundered. Instead, investigators would need additional evidence to show who specifically controlled which addresses.

Currently, investigators face a harder task of transitioning from tracing stolen funds to identifying those responsible.

While blockchain records indicate how Binance hacked funds moved about in terms of laundering and money laundering, they do not indicate who was ultimately directing the hack.

Therefore, investigators will need to determine if any of the wallets are connected to the previous work of North Korea-related groups. Possible sources of data that can aid investigators in determining this include malware samples, server logs, and IP addresses.

Meanwhile, exchange records may reveal where the attackers attempted to convert or withdraw the stolen assets. These findings could turn the FBI’s attribution into a stronger case for accountability.

Without independent forensic evidence and international cooperation, however, proving direct state involvement remains difficult.

The FBI blamed North Korea for the $6.3 billion Binance hack, but Pyongyang denies it.

Blockchain trails reveal widespread laundering, but North Korea’s role remains unproven.

#5288. Social Security November Payments: Why Dates Shifted This Month

Home » Blitz news » Social Security November Payments: Why Dates Shifted This Month

November’s payment calendar includes an early SSI deposit, a Veterans Day adjustment and four scheduled Social Security distribution dates.

Millions of Americans receiving Social Security and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits face an adjusted payment schedule this November. Due to a federal holiday and calendar shifts, several payment groups will receive their deposits earlier than expected.

Crucially, Supplemental Security Income (SSI) recipients will not receive a payment in November, as their monthly distribution was issued on Friday, October 30.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) distributes regular monthly benefits across four specific dates in November:

The primary schedule shift in November involves Veterans Day, observed on Wednesday, November 11.

Because federal offices and banking institutions close for federal holidays, beneficiaries born between the 1st and 10th—who normally receive funds on the second Wednesday of the month—will have their direct deposits issued one day early on Tuesday, November 10.

All subsequent birthday groups (Nov. 18 and Nov. 25) will receive payments on their regular Wednesday schedule.

Federal law mandates electronic payment via direct deposit or the Direct Express Debit Mastercard. Most deposits post by 9:00 a.m. local time on the payment date. If an expected check is missing, beneficiaries are advised to contact their financial institution before calling the SSA helpline.

November’s payment schedule is not the only development beneficiaries should watch.

In addition to November payment updates, the SSA has finalized a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027.

The 3.6% adjustment raises average monthly retirement checks by approximately $75 per month starting in January 2027. SSI recipients will receive their updated January 2027 payment early on December 31, 2026, as January 1 is a federal holiday.

Beneficiaries with personal my Social Security accounts will also be able to access their personalized COLA notices online starting in late November. Paper notices are expected to arrive in December.

Social Security and SSI payments are a steady source of cash flow for millions of Americans. Knowing the exact dates helps recipients plan spending, including any money they allocate to investments.

#5285. BTCPay Server Tells Merchants to Shut Down After Attackers Sweep Hot Wallets: Are Payments Still Safe?

Bitcoin news: BTCPay Server told merchants to go offline after attackers swept hot wallets on 2.4.1 or older. Here is who is exposed.

In today’s Bitcoin news, BTCPay Server, the free open-source payment processor many Bitcoin merchants run themselves, told every operator to shut down their instance after reports that attackers were sweeping the hot wallets on merchant servers. Less than six hours later, the culprit was old software.

At 04:07 UTC on Monday, the project said its investigation had found an attack vector aimed at servers running version 2.4.1, released on July 23, or older. It has “no credible reports” of drains on the current 2.4.7. BTCPay has not said how much was stolen or how many stores were hit.

That makes this a different kind of Bitcoin news from last week’s Binance hack. No exchange was breached. Merchants who run their own payment stack, the people self-custody is meant to protect, were the target.

So who was exposed, and what should store owners do now?

Unauthorized attackers are reportedly draining hot wallets on @BtcpayServer instances.

Users running BTCPay Server instances are advised to shut them down immediately. pic.twitter.com/H7mXfJLLcD

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 2, 2026

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

An attacker logged in as admin on older servers and emptied the hot wallets. BTCPay Server raised the alarm at 22:25 UTC on Sunday and asked operators to run its shutdown script “until we complete the investigation.”

Two hours later, founder Nicolas Dorier said the project’s own public servers on 2.4.7 were not attacked. “The attacker managed to log in as admin on those instance, we are still trying to figure out how,” he wrote.

📢 Our incident response investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running versions 2.4.1 (Jul 23, 2026) or older.

We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release. We again urge everyone to keep their BTCPay Server… pic.twitter.com/gYxK4Bb7fc

— BTCPay Server (@BtcpayServer) November 2, 2026

A hot wallet keeps its signing keys on the server itself, so it can pay out refunds and payouts automatically. Anyone with admin rights on that server can send the coins too.

Hosting providers moved fast. BTCPay thanked LunaNode and others for shutting down older hosted instances on their own, so some merchants may find their store offline on Monday.

The version history is the story. 2.4.1 shipped on July 23. Two weeks later, 2.4.2 fixed a critical flaw the team said was “being actively exploited,” and five more releases followed, ending with Thursday’s 2.4.7, which fixed 85 findings from an AI security scan Anthropic ran for the project.

Whether this is the same hole as August’s is still open. Dorier said a blog post with more detail is coming.

Only if it still runs 2.4.1 or older, on what the project knows so far. “For those who already updated at least once since the release of 2.4.2, there is no reason to panic,” Dorier wrote at 04:10 UTC.

The reported drains all hit hot wallets. Stores that receive into a watch-only wallet keep their signing keys off the server altogether.

#5284. Mercado Bitcoin hack: Attacker still holds PEPE, AAVE, and PENDLE as millions remain exposed

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

A major security breach occurred on the Mercado Bitcoin exchange. Hackers stole about $46 million in cryptocurrencies. After the exploit, investigators were able to track all the stolen money through 65 different addresses.

The most significant amount was held in an Ethereum [ETH] account valued at about $8.26 million.

Bitcoin [BTC] trailed closely with 106.068 BTC, worth approximately $8.1 million.

The wallets also contain $5.03 million in Tether [USDT] and $3.03 million in USD Coin [USDC]. Meanwhile, more than $9 million in stolen assets have been frozen.

However, the hacker’s remaining balances leave several tokens exposed to further transfers, laundering attempts, and potential selling pressure.

Although investigators have frozen more than $9 million, the attacker still controls substantial altcoin balances. Because the attacker can no longer access much of the stolen funds due to the frozen assets.

However, this does create the potential for another type of market risk. Instead, this shifts the focus to where the attacker ultimately transfers those tokens, whether to an exchange or one or more DeFi platforms.

PePe [PEPE], Aave [AAVE], and Pendle [PENDLE] each represent more than 80% of that total and carry the most risk since they would be transferred into relatively illiquid areas of the market.

The values of those tokens are approximately $1.79 million, $1.61 million, and $1.39 million, respectively.

The attacker also appears to hold very significant positions in Uniswap [UNI] and Ondo [ONDO]. If such tokens are sent to trading venues, large sell orders could overwhelm existing liquidity.

As such, could result in even steeper declines in thinner markets while causing even greater uncertainty for token holders who may expect subsequent transfers.

The key risk now lies in how easily the hacker could sell the remaining tokens without disrupting their markets. Despite PEPE and AAVE having higher token balances being stolen from them, each platform has greater than $230 million in daily trading volume.

Therefore, a concentrated sale could potentially overwhelm existing liquidity. In turn, this would lead to steeper declines in price than if that same sale had taken place in a token with deeper liquidity.

Meanwhile, the absence of confirmed exchange deposits suggests the hacker has not yet begun large-scale liquidation. However, any movement toward trading platforms could increase volatility, particularly for PENDLE, where market depth offers less protection.

The Mercado Bitcoin hack involved approximately $46 million in stolen cryptocurrency, with investigators freezing over $9 million.

The attacker retains millions in PEPE, AAVE, PENDLE, and other altcoins, leaving their markets exposed to potential sell-offs.

As per the latest recovery update from Binance, the exchange began its second significant withdrawal restoration phase at 04:00 UTC on Nov. 3.

Apart from RLUSD, the cryptocurrency exchange is now gradually re-enabling withdrawals for dozens of cryptocurrencies on multiple blockchain networks, including Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, XRP Ledger, Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron and Base.

For Ethereum, the list of cryptocurrencies now available for withdrawal includes Shiba Inu (SHIB), Chainlink (LINK), Worldcoin (WLD), Ondo (ONDO) and Ethena (ENA).

At the same time, the cryptocurrency exchange has also added XRP and a number of other top crypto assets to its list of withdrawals that will soon be re-enabled on BNB Smart Chain.

The crypto exchange emphasized that not all of the listed assets will be enabled for withdrawal at once. Instead, each asset and network combination will be re-enabled individually after the necessary security and operational checks are completed.

“We will gradually re-enable more assets & networks in stages once we complete the relevant security checks,” Binance said.

At the same time, the crypto exchange also warned that there may be delays due to traffic during this restoration process. Meanwhile, cryptocurrency deposits remain functional.

Initially, Binance started re-enabling withdrawals on Nov. 1 for top cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), XRP, Solana (SOL), Dogecoin (DOGE) and Zcash (ZEC), as well as major stablecoins USDT and USDC.

The latest withdrawal restoration update comes only a few days after the cryptocurrency exchange suffered a massive hack on Oct. 29, which resulted in the theft of about $6.3 billion in crypto.

The FBI officially identified the perpetrators of the hack as North Korean hackers linked to the infamous TraderTraitor operation on Oct. 31.

The U.S. agency revealed that hackers have been converting stolen cryptocurrencies mostly into Ethereum as a potential path toward laundering the assets through decentralized finance platforms and crypto swap services.

More withdrawal restorations will follow as Binance moves forward with its security checks and recovery processes.

#5281. XRP Targets Stripe’s $1.9 Trillion Payments Ecosystem as Ripple Integrates Privy Wallets

Ripple is expanding the XRP Ledger’s (XRPL) reach into digital payments through a partnership with Privy, the embedded wallet provider owned by Stripe.

Announced Tuesday, the integration will let developers build applications that support XRP, Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin, and other digital assets without requiring users to manage cryptocurrency wallets independently.

Notably, the partnership could make it easier for fintech companies to incorporate blockchain-based payments into their products, potentially giving XRP greater exposure to Stripe’s payments ecosystem. Stripe reported $1.9 trillion in payment volume during 2025, a 34% increase from the previous year, according to its annual update.

However, it’s important to note that, while the integration does not mean Stripe will process payments in XRP, it could broaden the asset’s reach by making XRPL-based applications easier to develop.  Under the agreement, developers can create wallets, sign transactions, and build services using XRP, RLUSD, and other supported assets.

Privy provides ready-made wallet tools that businesses can integrate into their apps, while allowing users to export their private keys and recovery phrases.

“Privy brings proven wallet infrastructure that makes it easier for fintechs and developers to bring XRPL into real products, from payments and stablecoin experiences to emerging forms of agentic commerce.” Markus Infanger, senior vice president of RippleX at Ripple said.

The companies also plan to introduce policy controls and gas sponsorship, giving developers more control over transactions while simplifying the payment process for users.

These features could support agentic commerce, where artificial intelligence agents make payments to purchase digital services or complete tasks. Privy’s server-side wallets would allow these agents to hold and transfer funds, while support for internet native payments (x402 payments) could enable automated transactions between online services.

For businesses that prefer to avoid cryptocurrency price volatility, the integration also supports RLUSD, Ripple’s dollar-pegged stablecoin. This could allow developers to build payment applications using a stable-value digital asset rather than relying solely on XRP.

Ripple’s move comes as competing blockchain networks pursue partnerships with established financial providers.  Just last month, the Cardano Foundation joined Mastercard’s Crypto Partner Program to explore blockchain applications across payments and financial services.

Cardano has also pursued stablecoin liquidity through USDCx and institutional asset support through Fireblocks, while its participation in the x402 ecosystem targets automated payments involving AI agents.

Ripple, meanwhile, has expanded its payment partnerships through a March 2025 collaboration with Chipper Cash to support crypto-enabled cross-border payments into Africa. In November 2025, Ripple, Mastercard, WebBank, and Gemini announced a collaboration to explore RLUSD settlement for Gemini credit card transactions.

#5279. Coinbase Data Shows XRP May See 8.7% Price Move

Options market data for cryptocurrencies published by major US crypto exchange Coinbase indicates that a big (approximately 8.7%) price swing for XRP could be expected by Nov. 8.

At the time of writing, XRP and Solana are tied in terms of the biggest expected price move (according to options-implied volatility), both showing an 8.7% expected move.

Ethereum (ETH) has an expected 7.7% move. Meanwhile, Bitcoin (BTC) is the asset with the lowest expected price move (according to implied volatility) among the top four assets (5.8%).

It is important to note that the above numbers do not necessarily mean that a big upward move in the price of XRP is expected.

They only mean that options traders are expecting significant moves (up or down).

According to Coinbase data, an 8.7% price move (up or down) could be possible within the specified timeframe.

The current price of XRP is around $1.25.

An 8.7% move up would mean the price of XRP could reach around $1.36.

An 8.7% move down would mean the price of XRP could reach around $1.14.

That would mean the implied price range for XRP is around 1.14–1.36.

It is worth noting that Coinbase's numbers are based on "implied volatility," which is a measure based on options prices that reflects the market's expectations for future price swings.

Coinbase is referring to a "one standard deviation" or 1σ move. In the typical normal distribution context, this means there's about a 68% chance that the asset will end up in the specified range.

That does not mean XRP will necessarily be in that price range, nor that there's a 50/50 chance of an 8.7% rally or fall.

What it means is that the options market provides an estimate of the size of the expected move, but it does not necessarily indicate the direction of the move.

#5277. Hedera’s Banking Push Leaves HBAR Waiting For Demand

Home » Trendsetter News » Hedera’s Banking Push Leaves HBAR Waiting For Demand

Hedera’s banking integrations are expanding, but a rapid demand rise for HBAR remains unproven.

Hedera collects only a few hundred dollars in network fees on a typical day despite HBAR’s multibillion-dollar valuation, according to an analyst examining the gap between institutional adoption and token demand.

Fire Hustle’s central question is whether banks using Hedera will need meaningful HBAR holdings – or simply benefit from its inexpensive infrastructure.

The analyst points to Taurus integrating Hedera into a platform serving more than 40 banks and regulated institutions. That gives those clients access to HBAR custody, staking and token issuance, but access is not evidence that banks have launched products or accumulated tokens.

Hedera denominates transaction fees in dollars and collects payment in HBAR. When the token’s price rises, fewer tokens are needed to cover the same dollar-denominated charge.

That makes costs predictable for businesses. It also weakens the assumption that rising transaction counts must produce proportionately stronger token demand, particularly when fees remain small.

“Who has to hold HBAR and how much,” the analyst asks. The video identifies staking and operational token inventories as possible demand sources, although it does not establish how much HBAR institutions would need to retain.

The infrastructure argument centers on CLPR, which the video describes as technology allowing networks to verify one another’s records cryptographically without an intermediary holding funds.

According to Fire Hustle, Hashgraph contributed it to the Linux Foundation and opened an early-adopter program targeting payments, foreign exchange and collateral movement.

She highlights Swift and Wells Fargo joining the foundation on the same day as the contribution. But the qualification matters: “There’s no official announcement that Swift is using Clipper.” Shared foundation membership does not establish a deployment.

The video also places Hedera among participants in a UK tokenization initiative, citing a live on-chain repo trial targeted for April 2027 and led by BlackRock and NatWest. It does not establish that Hedera or CLPR will power that trial; other named participants include Ripple, Coinbase and Circle.

#5275. Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 in 2026, More Than Triple 2025, Yet Without Binance the Year Ran Quieter: How Did Bitcoin and Ethereum React After Major Hacks?

Crypto hack losses hit $8.74B in 2026 vs $2.51B in 2025. Here’s how Bitcoin and Ether moved a day, a week and a month after major hacks.

Crypto hack losses reached $8.74 billion in 2026 by October 31, more than three times the $2.51 billion lost over the same ten months of 2025, after the October 29 Binance breach alone added $6.36 billion.

Take Binance out and the picture flips. The rest of 2026 comes to $2.38 billion, about 5% less than 2025 at the same point, even though attackers hit 325 targets against 120 a year earlier. More attacks, smaller hauls, and then one enormous one.

The market has its own pattern. Across the ten largest hacks since January 2025, Bitcoin’s move on the day of the attack ranged from -4.1% to +1.9%. A month later, for the nine with a full month of data, the range ran from -15.5% to +19.9%, and it followed whatever the broader market was doing.

The 2025 hacks landed in falling markets, and every one was followed by a lower Bitcoin price a month later. Most of 2026’s landed in rising ones.

So how bad has 2026 really been, and what does history say about the weeks after Binance?

The size of the biggest theft. Through September, 2026 was running behind 2025: $2.24 billion lost against $2.48 billion. Then Binance lost $6.36 billion across ten blockchains in one night, more than all of 2025’s hacks put together.

The two years share a culprit. The FBI tied 2025’s largest crypto hack, the $1.4 billion Bybit theft on February 21, to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Chainalysis now ties Binance to the same unit. The biggest hacks of each year:

The rest of 2026 looks different from 2025 too. There were 325 incidents through October, almost three times 2025’s 120, and five 2026 hacks topped $290 million, against one in 2025. Stolen keys and cross-chain bridges did most of the damage outside Binance.

The gross number also overstates what stays lost. CertiK’s October tally counts $3.03 billion frozen or returned, mostly Binance funds caught on-chain, which cuts the month’s adjusted losses to about $3.47 billion. Trackers also disagree on the year: CertiK puts 2026 at $9.2 billion gross and 2025 at $3.35 billion, while DefiLlama has $8.74 billion and $2.72 billion.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

A small dip on the day, then the market’s own trend. The heatmap compares Bitcoin and Ether with their close the day before each of the ten biggest hacks since 2025.

Bybit is the closest match to Binance: a North Korean exchange theft over $1 billion. Bitcoin lost 14.2% within a week of it, with US tariff fears weighing on markets that week too, and it was still 12.4% lower a month on.

Binance is following a gentler path so far. From the October 28 close to Monday:

Neither yet. Bitcoin trades at $77,870 on Binance, flat on the day, and has held above its October 30 low of $76,326 for three days, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average) at $76,512.

After Bybit, Bitcoin lost its floor within a week. After most of 2026’s hacks, it was higher a month later. The line between the two is clear on the chart: the 200-day EMA below, and the 50-day EMA at $80,293 above.

The crypto hack record says the first day rarely decides much. What Bitcoin does at the 200-day EMA over the next few weeks will show which path this one takes.

#5273. Binance Draws $2.3 Billion Inflows After Record $6.3 Billion Hack

Home » Exchanges » Binance News » Binance Draws $2.3 Billion Inflows After Record $6.3 Billion Hack

Binance’s trading volume orchestrates a rapid comeback as $2.3 billion inflows hit the recovering platform.

Binance has swung back to net inflows of roughly $2.3 billion over 24 hours after beginning to restore customer access following a security breach estimated at roughly $6.3 billion, according to market-tracking data. The reversal came after a period of heavy withdrawals and reflects an early, if incomplete, return of confidence in the exchange.

The incident is being described as the largest theft in crypto’s history. Binance said its initial investigation found that a compromised laptop used by a DevOps engineer enabled unauthorized withdrawals of Bitcoin, Ether and other assets across multiple networks.

Efforts to contain the stolen assets have focused on tracing wallets and blocking transfers across the industry. Estimates of the amount frozen vary, but reports indicate that between roughly $2.7 billion and $3 billion of the funds were stopped or restricted shortly after the hacking incident.

JUST IN: 🚨 Binance net inflows flip positive as market activity surges.The exchange records a massive $2.3 billion in net inflows amid expanding user withdrawals.$BNB #Binance #Crypto

Ripple also said it froze $200 million in RLUSD connected to wallets linked to the suspected exploit. The intervention highlighted the role that issuers of centrally administered stablecoins can play in limiting the movement of funds after a major breach.

Binance has said it will cover customer losses. The exchange’s reopening of withdrawals appears to have been the critical test: hourly deposits began exceeding withdrawals as access expanded, and Binance led centralized exchanges in net inflows during the latest 24-hour period.

BNB sold off sharply after the hack, at one point falling about 8.7% within an hour. The token was hit harder than several other large cryptocurrencies because of its direct connection to the Binance ecosystem, even though the reported exploit did not target BNB Chain itself.

Futures positioning also turned more defensive, with funding rates slipping negative as traders increased short exposure. BNB later found support near its 200-day moving average, but it remains below pre-hack levels and faces resistance around the $733 area cited by technical analysts.

The broader crypto market has stayed under pressure, with Bitcoin near $77,000 and several major altcoins recording steeper monthly declines. Risk appetite has been strained by exchange-traded fund outflows, geopolitical concerns and uncertainty around monetary policy, magnifying the shock from the Binance breach.

#5272. XRP Defies Bear Market: New Wallets Double Despite Price Pressure

The XRP Ledger network recorded the largest capital migration in recent months. According to the Santiment platform, on Sunday, November 1, users created 7,934 new wallets. This is the sixth-largest daily result in all of 2026, which, moreover, occurred on a weekend — traditionally the most passive period for blockchain networks.

The influx of new addresses more than doubled the autumn average of 3,500 wallets.

The surge in activity was a direct reaction to the hack of the Binance exchange on October 29. During the attack on the platform’s hot wallets, hackers, whom the FBI links to the North Korean group TraderTraitor, stole assets worth $6.36 billion. Also falling into their hands were 233 million XRP tokens (about $297 million).

Instead of panic selling, investors began saving their capital. The mass opening of addresses is a consequence of withdrawing tokens from the centralized platform to independent “cold” wallets (self-custody). Investors are taking control of their private keys and distributing risks by transferring coins to clean, newly created addresses.

This behavior reflects growing distrust of centralized custodians, as even the largest exchanges remain vulnerable to sophisticated attacks.

Despite the fact that a huge volume of XRP ended up under the hackers’ control, the market held up. The price found strong support at the $1.20 level and is now consolidating around $1.25. Such resilience suggests that holders view the incident as an exchange-specific problem rather than a threat to the XRP Ledger itself.

A rare precedent has emerged on the market: XRP’s on-chain metrics are growing despite external stress and a price lull. If the influx of new wallets holds above 4,000 per day, buyers will have a strong foundation for betting on a rise.

The first signal for growth will be the price consolidating above the $1.30 resistance. If, however, network optimism fades and daily growth falls below 3,000 addresses, the asset will return to a prolonged flat phase.

#5271. Binance restores access across nine networks – Can deposits keep pace with exits?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

After the $6.3 billion hack, which shook the entire community, Binance has resumed cryptocurrency withdrawals for several major digital assets.

This includes Bitcoin [BTC], Ethereum [ETH], Ripple [XRP], Solana [SOL], Dogecoin [DOGE], Chainlink [LINK], Cardano [ADA], Litecoin [LTC], and Shiba Inu [SHIB].

According to the exchange’s announcement, withdrawals for these assets reopened at 04:00 UTC on the 3rd of November across nine supported networks.

That said, the exchange has also begun restoring withdrawals for selected assets across additional networks, including Sui, Arbitrum, Optimism, TRON, and Base. However, the process will take place gradually as Binance completes its security checks across different networks and assets.

Remarking on the same, the Binance team noted,

We are prioritizing tokens based on user demand over the past week, restoring each network-asset pair carefully after completing rigorous security checks. Additional assets will be added as they become ready.

Adding more to this, one of CryptQuant’s analysts noted,

Withdrawals are being processed correctly, with no further security issues and today shows a net outflow totaling -16,021 BTC so far.

This coincided with AMBCrypto’s recent report that Binance witnessed significant withdrawal activity after reopening its services on the 1st of November. In fact, within the first two hours, users withdrew approximately $733 million worth of assets. All in all, the exchange has replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets using its own funds.

They further confirmed that BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC are fully backed at a minimum 1:1 ratio.

Although the large outflows raised concerns about customer confidence, continued deposits and gradually declining withdrawal volumes suggested that activity was slowly normalizing.

Now, while Binance buckles up to resume activity after the hack, the exchange also recorded approximately $3.29 billion in net outflows over the past 24 hours, marking a decline of more than 50% from its earlier intraday peak of nearly $7 billion, according to DeFiLlama data.

The decline suggests that the initial rush to move funds away from Binance may be easing following the reported security breach. Meanwhile, the exchange’s remaining on-chain holdings stood at approximately $127.78 billion.

This comes on the heels of Binance’s latest Proof of Reserves (PoR) report, dated 31st October, which revealed changes in the cryptocurrency holdings maintained by users on the exchange.

The most notable development was a sharp decline in USDT balances, alongside falling Ethereum and BNB holdings. However, Bitcoin holdings recorded a slight increase.

However, fear still remains, as the Binance hacker has reportedly started mixing stolen cryptocurrency to make the funds harder to trace.

So far, the stolen assets have passed through approximately 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchain networks in more than 40,000 transactions. Lastly, around $3.24 billion remains in theft-linked addresses, primarily in Bitcoin and Ethereum, while approximately $2.85 billion has been frozen.

#5268. Tether holds about 150,000 Bitcoin, Ardoino says—What do its reserves show?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

During a Plan ₿ Forum presentation in Lugano, Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino indicated the company owns nearly 150,000 Bitcoin. That amount would be worth about $11.5 billion with the Bitcoin price reported on November 3.

This figure is higher than Tether’s most recent USDT reserve disclosure, as the number shows its broader Bitcoin exposure.

“We have give or take 150,000 bitcoin ourselves,” Ardoino said, according to his disclosure during his speech at the Lugano event. He discussed the holdings while outlining Tether’s support for Bitcoin and its mining investments.

Ardoino did not give any acquisition schedule or breakdown identifying which Tether entities hold the coins. The timing and composition of the approximately 150,000 BTC position, therefore, remain unclear.

Tether has pursued Bitcoin purchases for several years. About three years ago, it announced its plans to start allocating, regularly, up to 15% of its net realized operating profits to Bitcoin.

Tether published its latest reserve report, providing a view of its USDT reserves. The company released the reserves of its latest report [for September 30] on October 30.

It lists around $8.37 billion in Bitcoin, and with today’s valuation per coin, the firm holds roughly 100,060 BTC.

Tether has long-term proprietary investments that are held separately from token reserves. Ardoino’s presentation has not made the connection between these investment returns and his Bitcoin estimate clear, yet.

There is roughly 50,000 BTC remaining unaccounted for between the CEO’s 200,000 to 220,000 BTC approximation vs the reserve report at face value.

Bitcoin holdings constitute part of Tether’s reserve portfolio. Its direct and indirect exposure to U.S. Treasury bills reached $132.4 billion at the end of September.

The total reserve assets was $191.45 billion, with liabilities amounting to $183.50 billion. The net surplus reached about $7.95 billion, a notable increase from $4.11 billion in June.

#5267. After 24 Million Launches, Just 312 Memecoins Are Above $100,000

Home » Altcoins » After 24 Million Launches, Just 312 Memecoins Are Above $100,000

The rarest breed of meme currencies launched on Pump.Fun stay above a $100,000 market capitalization.

Pump.fun’s explosive memecoin-creation activity is colliding with a stark outcome: of roughly 24 million launches on the platform, only 312 tokens have climbed above a $100,000 valuation threshold. The gap has sharpened scrutiny of how much lasting value the memecoin launchpad is producing.

The numbers underscore the extreme attrition built into rapid-fire token launches. Vast volumes of new memecoins can create attention and trading bursts, but only a tiny fraction appear to develop enough liquidity, demand or staying power to clear even relatively modest valuation levels.

Pump.fun has become closely associated with the low-cost, high-speed creation of memecoins. That model can lower barriers for creators and traders, while also producing an overwhelming supply of projects competing for the same pool of capital.

JUST IN: THERE HAVE BEEN 24.4M COINS LAUNCHED ON PUMPFUN312 ARE CURRENTLY ABOVE $100K MARKET CAP https://t.co/t0Qvv6Oqj3

With only 312 tokens reportedly surpassing $100,000 out of 24 million launches, the implied success rate is exceptionally small. The figure does not by itself establish whether individual launches were designed for long-term development, short-term trading or experimentation, but it highlights how quickly most tokens fade from view.

The DeFi platform is now facing broader questions about whether transaction activity and launch counts translate into a durable business model. High turnover may generate engagement, yet it can also leave traders exposed to thin liquidity and sharp price reversals once early interest disappears.

Concerns around memecoins have been amplified by the weak performance of PUMP amid softer market sentiment. When a platform-linked token struggles during a risk-off period, investors tend to look more closely at the underlying economics: user retention, trading demand and the quality of projects emerging from the ecosystem.

Pump.fun’s figures offer a blunt reminder for the wider crypto market: token creation is easy, but building liquidity and relevance is not. Investors weighing exposure to launchpad ecosystems will likely focus less on raw volume and more on whether those platforms can consistently produce assets that survive beyond the first burst of speculation.

In a recent X discussion, Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has clarified his current position at the company.

An X user had asked Schwartz whether he still serves as a non-executive director. "Are you not still a Non-Executive Director at Ripple?" the X user asked.

The question came after Schwartz said he no longer works for Ripple and had retired. "I don't work for Ripple anymore. I retired," Schwartz stated.In response to the X user's question, Schwartz said he remains on Ripple's Board of Directors and also serves as CTO Emeritus: "I'm on the Board of Directors and I'm CTO Emeritus."

@Lebro589 @CocaColaKid_OG @Fernando031680 @jtraulf1 @SergioVengeance @MAGASouthEastFL @Emmaiid11 I'm on the Board of Directors and I'm CTO Emeritus. I still meet with my former team twice a month and show up randomly at Ripple offices and say "hi".

Schwartz also said he still meets with his former team twice a month, while he occasionally visits Ripple's offices without a formal schedule, describing these visits as opportunities to say hello to his former colleagues: "I still meet with my former team twice a month and show up randomly at Ripple offices and say hi."

David Schwartz, one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger, became the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) of Ripple in July 2018, after previously serving as the company's chief cryptographer since 2011. He transitioned out of his day-to-day operating CTO role at the end of December 2025 to become CTO Emeritus and join Ripple's Board of Directors.

Despite stepping away from his full-time responsibilities, Schwartz indicated that he maintains a connection with the company and his former team.

Schwartz maintains he was not going away from the XRP community, participating in the XRP Ledger through his XRP node, which has now been running for several months, publishing its output data and researching other use cases for XRP besides what Ripple is focused on, among other things.

Shortly after Evernorth, a Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm, was revealed, Schwartz stated he would serve as a strategic advisor to the company, bringing his wealth of experience despite his retirement from Ripple.

At the Swell event, which was held at the end of October, Schwartz joined Ayo Akinyele, Head of Engineering for RippleX, in a conversation on what comes next for XRPL. The discussion explored the technologies shaping the ledger's evolution, the trade-offs behind them, and what it will take to support the next generation of financial and on-chain applications.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Ethereum [ETH] exchange reserves dropped to their lowest levels since 2016, raising hopes of a supply-driven recovery despite the prevailing market weakness.

According to CryptoQuant Community insights, the total ETH exchange reserves declined to roughly 14.5 million ETH on November 2. This decline reportedly marked a 58.6% reduction from the 2020 peak of 35 million ETH.

Over that period, the exchanges have in fact lost around 20.5 million ETH from their cumulative balances.

Notably, Binance registered a similar drop, with reserves falling 37.1% from their 2025 peak of 4.9 million ETH, with its holdings reaching 3.08 million ETH, revisiting levels last seen in late 2020.

It is also worth noting that the reserve drop also coincided with reports of Binance’s October 29 hack, which allegedly caused significant losses.

For context, these security concerns could have encouraged investors to transfer their holdings into self-custody wallets, rather than necessarily indicating stronger accumulation or renewed buying demand.

Institutional accumulation has also strengthened despite the token’s recent struggles, with Tom Lee’s Bitmine expanding its ETH holdings.

Lookonchain recently reported on X that Bitmine purchased another 5,000 ETH valued roughly $11.22 million, bringing the total acquisition to 6.065 million ETH, worth nearly $13.7 billion.

The institution now controls around 4.96% of Ethereum’s total supply, strengthening its significant exposure to the asset.

Meanwhile, CoinGlass analytics highlighted that Ethereum’s Spot netflows remained negative, registering approximately $7.91 million in net outflows at press time.

Bitmine’s continued purchases, together with the negative Spot netflows, reinforced the declining immediate selling pressure picture.

Traders on the derivatives market also showed renewed optimism despite Ethereum’s recent market weakness. In particular, ETH’s OI-Weighted Funding Rate had recovered to 0.0101% at press time, returning to positive territory after an earlier brief negative reading.

This recovery implied that long traders were paying shorts, which reflected fresh demand for bullish leveraged positions.

Besides, Binance’s top trader Long/Short Ratio revealed a considerable preference for long positions, with the long accounts representing 70.2% of top traders, compared to 29.8% holding short positions.

These readings together suggested that market participants were increasingly optimistic for price recovery despite the prevailing downward trend.

Ethereum’s defense of the $2,243 support level validated the hopes of a price rebound despite the prevailing bearish market outlook.

Following the defense, Ethereum’s market value sat at $2,254 as of writing time, positioning itself around the middle of its descending channel.

More importantly, the RSI indicator stood at 33.23, approaching oversold conditions and raising the possibility of selling exhaustion.

The Money Flow Index (MFI) meanwhile reached 37.18, highlighting relatively weak capital inflows despite the successful defense of the support level.

Overall, Ethereum’s declining exchange reserves, Bitmine accumulation, and bullish derivatives positioning favored the possibility of a rebound.

A continued buying above $2,243 could strengthen that outlook, while reclaiming the $2,385 resistance would provide stronger confirmation of a sustained recovery.

#5263. Bitcoin ETF Outflows Hit $398.6M on November 2 as BlackRock Leads Redemptions

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded a combined $398.6 million net outflow on November 2, according to Farside Investors’ daily fund table. These figures are dated November 2.

The November 2 figure also followed a larger $643.2 million net outflow on October 30 in Farside’s table. Back-to-back negative sessions invite closer scrutiny of allocation decisions, but they do not reveal the identities or intentions of the underlying investors. That is why the per-issuer breakdown deserves at least as much attention as the headline total.

US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded a combined $398.6 million net outflow on November 2, according to Farside Investors’ daily fund table. BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for about $405.3 million of redemptions, while Fidelity’s FBTC received roughly $6.7 million. The net result therefore masks a small positive contribution outside the largest fund, rather than a perfectly uniform exit from every issuer. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

An ETF flow number measures creations minus redemptions in a fund, not the amount of Bitcoin traded on every exchange during a session. It also does not establish whether a holder moved into cash, shifted to another wrapper or rebalanced a portfolio. The transactions are economically connected to underlying Bitcoin exposure, but the relationship between a reported flow and intraday spot prices is not a simple one-for-one equation.

The concentration is the important detail here. When one large product accounts for more than the market-wide outflow, investors should be cautious about turning the aggregate number into a claim about all institutional accounts. A multi-day pattern across issuers would say more about appetite than one concentrated day. Flows can still influence sentiment because ETFs have become a visible channel for regulated Bitcoin exposure.

Fund flows and corporate Bitcoin holdings share one characteristic: they are easy to count and harder to interpret. A securities wrapper reports its own creations and redemptions; a public company reports transactions inside a particular capital structure. Neither dataset captures every spot-market participant. A useful analysis establishes the reporting date, identifies what was measured and asks how much the disclosed activity represents relative to the wider market.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: the previous Bitcoin and Ether ETF flow review and BlackRock’s October Bitcoin ETF inflow against peer withdrawals. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

These figures are dated November 2. They are not a live reading of November 3 subscriptions, nor are they a forecast of the next trading session. A net redemption does not by itself prove forced liquidation or financial stress at the fund. Market makers and authorised participants manage inventory, and fund-level flows are just one part of the wider liquidity picture.

The critical operational issue is access to liquid Bitcoin exposure. A fund shareholder may own a listed security, while a corporate treasury holder owns shares in a company with liabilities and management decisions. Those two instruments can behave differently even when Bitcoin is the most visible asset behind both. Treating the wrapper as identical to the coin erases meaningful risks.

Watch whether IBIT redemptions persist across subsequent sessions, whether other large issuers follow and whether the move coincides with a material change in spot liquidity. The more convincing signal would be several days of broad participation. Until then, it is better to describe this as a sharp, concentrated withdrawal from US-listed Bitcoin funds rather than a verdict on the entire asset class.

#5262. No Ethereum (ETH)? Exchanges Report Substantial Outflows

Ethereum’s exchange supply is shrinking after the October 29 Binance hack, but on-chain data suggests there is something more interesting hiding behind the scenes. The two-stage decline in exchange-held ETH could reflect the liquidity contraction rather than a minor panic-fueled outflow.

Between October 28 and November 2, the share of Ethereum’s total supply held on exchanges dropped from 3.56% to 3.20%, a decline of 0.36%. Just over half of that drop happened on October 29, the same day as the reported Binance exploit.

According to TRM Labs, hackers drained around 200,630 ETH from Binance’s hot wallet.

Instead of dropping right away, ETH balances on top exchange addresses actually grew by around 39,000 ETH on October 29. The bigger drop came later. Those addresses lost roughly 313,000 ETH on November 1 and November 2, after withdrawals were reopened.

Major exchange addresses lost around 297,000 ETH, or 5.4%, between October 28 and November 2, suggesting a substantial liquidity thinning.

Falling exchange balances aren't necessarily suggesting an accumulation. The coins may have gone into cold storage, moved between wallets, or sent to other exchanges. Exchange-address data alone can’t show where they've been sent.

As of now, Ethereum’s price stays bearish. On the daily ETH/USD chart, ETH is trading near $2,264, below several key moving averages. The price has pulled back from its October highs around $2,800.

Selling pressure can be clearly seen on the chart, and the $2,300-$2,400 range could act as resistance. A proper recovery above the level would suggest an improvement in sentiment. But if buyers fail to defend the $2,200 area, Ethereum could drop even further.

For now, the current supply drop is more of a liquidity shift, rather than a confirmed supply shock, especially on gigantic exchanges like Binance.

The more important question is whether the missing ETH has actually left trading circulation or just moved elsewhere. Until market flows calm down a little, it’s too early to call the exchange supply drop a bullish signal.

TL;DR: US spot Ether ETFs saw approximately $139.7 million in net outflows on November 2, Farside Investors’ daily data show. The amounts are published for specific trading dates and can be adjusted by data providers.

On November 2, BlackRock’s ETHA was responsible for roughly $138.3 million of the reported net withdrawal. That clustering suggests the fund-level series deserves careful reading. Investors can track one issuer and the whole category without treating the two as interchangeable, particularly when other funds show smaller and sometimes opposite daily movements.

US spot Ether ETFs saw approximately $139.7 million in net outflows on November 2, Farside Investors’ daily data show. The previous listed sessions were also negative, with approximately $155.7 million leaving on October 30 and $105.5 million on October 29. The sequence offers a more informative starting point than any single day, although the scale of redemptions varies from session to session. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

ETH ETF flows are subscriptions and withdrawals through an investment wrapper, not a direct count of ETH sold by everyone in the ecosystem. Exchange traders, staking participants, derivatives desks and users of Ethereum applications have different motives and do not all appear in the same table. ETF holdings reflect a familiar securities-market channel that may lag or diverge from blockchain activity.

A series of negative sessions can change how investors talk about Ethereum exposure, especially when a large issuer accounts for most of a particular day’s redemptions. But a falling ETF share count and weaker network fundamentals are not synonymous. Analysts should compare flows with changes in broader risk appetite, fund allocations and the health of Ethereum-based services rather than assume one metric explains the others.

Ethereum has multiple sources of demand and risk: trading, staking, stablecoin settlement, application fees and long-term treasury allocation. A change in one part of that system should be tested against the others instead of promoted into a universal explanation. The market often overreacts when one publicly available metric is mistaken for the whole network economy.

For additional perspective, it is worth reading our existing reporting on an earlier Ethereum ETF outflow comparison and the October Bitcoin and Ether ETF weekly review. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

The amounts are published for specific trading dates and can be adjusted by data providers. They do not tell us who redeemed, whether positions were hedged or whether the cash moved to Bitcoin, other funds or unrelated assets. Nor does this table establish that protocol staking withdrawals caused the ETF activity; those are different processes with distinct timing and constraints.

For investors, the right comparison is between liquidity, expected holding period and obligations. Staked ETH, ETF shares and treasury holdings may all track the same underlying asset, but their exit routes and operating constraints differ. A useful report therefore asks not simply how much ETH is involved, but how readily the exposure can be changed when conditions deteriorate.

The next useful evidence is the issuer breakdown over several additional sessions, alongside spot-market depth and whether redemption pressure broadens. A return to sustained net creations would change the recent trend, but an isolated inflow would not erase the larger pattern. Investors should keep ETF demand separate from claims about Ethereum’s throughput, staking or rollup adoption.
